title.zh: 卷三百二十六 列傳第二百十四 外國七
title.raw: 卷三百二十六 列傳第二百十四 外國七 Volume 326 Biographies 214: Foreign States 7

sentences.zh: 古里

translations.literal: Guli
translations.idiomatic: Calicut

sentences.zh: 〈今印度科澤科德

translations.literal: 〈Today's Kozhikode in India
translations.idiomatic: 〈This is present-day Kozhikode in India

sentences.zh: 〈（又名“卡利卡特”）〉，

translations.literal: (also called "Calicut")〉,
translations.idiomatic: It is also known as Calicut)〉,

sentences.zh: 位於印度戲海岸。

translations.literal: located on the western coast of India.
translations.idiomatic: on the Malabar Coast of India.

sentences.zh: 鄭和第一次下西洋，於此立碑，曰：『其國去中國十萬餘裡，民物鹹若，熙皓同風，刻石於茲，永昭萬世。』

translations.literal: On his first voyage to the Western Ocean, Zheng He erected a stele here, which reads: 'This country is more than a hundred thousand li from China; its people and things are all alike; brightness and harmony share the same wind; this stone is carved here to shine for ten thousand generations.'』
translations.idiomatic: On his first voyage to the Western Ocean, Zheng He set up a stele here inscribed: 'This land lies more than a hundred thousand li from China; its people and customs mirror our own; under the same bright harmony we carve this stone, that it may shine through all ages.'

sentences.zh: 是為鄭和於國外最早建立的一塊碑。

translations.literal: This was the earliest stele Zheng He erected abroad.
translations.idiomatic: This was the earliest stele Zheng He erected outside China.

sentences.zh: 後，鄭和第七次下西洋，返航途中病逝於此〉，

translations.literal: Later, on his seventh voyage to the Western Ocean, he fell ill and died here on the homeward journey〉,
translations.idiomatic: Later, on his seventh voyage home across the Western Ocean, he fell ill and died here.)〉

sentences.zh: 西洋大國。

translations.literal: a great state of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: It was a great power of the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 西濱大海，南距柯枝國，北距狼奴兒國，東七百里距坎巴國。

translations.literal: To the west it borders the great sea; to the south it is seven hundred li from the state of Cochin; to the north from the state of Langnu'er; to the east seven hundred li from the state of Kanba.
translations.idiomatic: It lay on the open sea to the west, with Cochin to the south, Langnu'er to the north, and Kanba seven hundred li to the east.

sentences.zh: 自柯枝舟行三日可至，自錫蘭山十日可至，諸蕃要會也。

translations.literal: By boat from Cochin one could reach it in three days; from Ceylon in ten days. It was the chief meeting place of the various fan states.
translations.idiomatic: A three-day sail from Cochin or ten days from Ceylon brought one there; it was the great entrepôt of the maritime states.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年命中官尹慶奉詔撫諭其國，賚以彩幣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the emperor ordered the eunuch Yin Qing to carry an edict to console and instruct the country, bestowing colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 (1403) the emperor sent the eunuch Yin Qing with an edict to reassure the realm and gifted it patterned silks.

sentences.zh: 其酋沙米的喜遣使從慶入朝，貢方物。

translations.literal: Its chief Shamidixi sent envoys to follow Qing into court and present local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler Shamidixi sent envoys with Qing to the capital, bearing regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年達南京，封為國王，賜印誥及文綺諸物，遂比年入貢。

translations.literal: In the third year they reached Nanjing; he was enfeoffed as king and given a seal, patent of appointment, figured silks, and other things, and thereafter tribute came every year.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Nanjing in the third year; he was invested as king and granted a seal, patent, brocades, and other gifts, after which tribute arrived yearly.

sentences.zh: 鄭和亦數使其國。

translations.literal: Zheng He also several times dispatched missions to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He likewise visited the realm on repeated missions.

sentences.zh: 十三年偕柯枝、南渤利、甘巴裡、滿剌加諸國入貢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year it joined Cochin, Nanboli, Gambali, Malacca, and other states in presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year it sent tribute together with Cochin, Nanboli, Gambali, Malacca, and others.

sentences.zh: 十四年又偕爪哇、滿剌加、佔城、錫蘭山、木骨都束、溜山、南渤利、不剌哇、阿丹、蘇門答剌、麻木、剌撒、忽魯謨斯、柯枝、南巫裡、沙裡灣泥、彭亨諸國入貢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year it again joined Java, Malacca, Champa, Ceylon, Mogadishu, Liushan, Nanboli, Barawa, Aden, Samudra, Mombasa, Las'a, Hormuz, Cochin, Nanwuli, Sarafan, Pahang, and other states in presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year it again joined Java, Malacca, Champa, Ceylon, Mogadishu, Liushan, Nanboli, Barawa, Aden, Samudra, Mombasa, Las'a, Hormuz, Cochin, Nanwuli, Sarafan, Pahang, and the other realms in tribute.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸蕃使臣充斥於廷，以古裡大國，序其使者於首。

translations.literal: At that time envoys from the various fan states filled the court; because Guli was a great state, its envoys were ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from the maritime states thronged the court, and because Calicut was a great power its mission was placed at the head of the order.

sentences.zh: 十七年偕滿剌加十七國來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year it came to offer tribute together with Malacca and sixteen other states.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year it presented tribute alongside Malacca and sixteen other states.

sentences.zh: 十九年又偕忽魯謨斯等國入貢。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year it again joined Hormuz and other states in presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year it again sent tribute with Hormuz and other states.

sentences.zh: 二十一年復偕忽魯謨斯等國，遣使千二百人入貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year it again joined Hormuz and other states, sending twelve hundred persons as envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year it again joined Hormuz and others, dispatching twelve hundred envoys on a tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 時帝方出塞，敕皇太子曰：「天時向寒，貢使即令禮官宴勞，給賜遣還。

translations.literal: The emperor was then campaigning beyond the frontier and instructed the crown prince: 'The season is turning cold; let the tribute envoys at once be entertained and rewarded by the ritual officials, given gifts, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was on campaign beyond the passes and wrote to the crown prince: 'Cold weather is setting in; have the ritual officials feast and reward the tribute envoys, grant them gifts, and send them home.

sentences.zh: 其以土物來市者，官酬其直。」

translations.literal: Those who have come to market local goods—the officials shall pay them fair value.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever has brought native goods to sell, let the officials pay them at fair price.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年，其王比裡麻遣使偕蘇門答剌等國使臣入貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xuande its king Bilima sent envoys together with envoys from Samudra and other states to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 8 (1433) King Bilima sent envoys with those from Samudra and other states to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 其使入留都下，正統元年乃命附爪哇貢舟西還。

translations.literal: Its envoys entered and remained in the capital; only in the first year of Zhengtong were they ordered to return west on Java's tribute vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Those envoys stayed on in the capital and were not sent home until Zhengtong 1 (1436), when they were told to sail west on Java's tribute ship.

sentences.zh: 自是不復至。

translations.literal: From then on they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: After that no further missions arrived.

sentences.zh: 其國，山多地瘠，有谷無麥。

translations.literal: Its country has many mountains and much poor soil; it has grain but no wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The land is mountainous and lean, with grain crops but no wheat.

sentences.zh: 俗甚淳，行者讓道，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: Its customs are very pure: travelers yield the road, and nothing lost on the road is picked up.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were notably upright: wayfarers gave way to one another, and lost goods were left untouched on the road.

sentences.zh: 人分五等，如柯枝，其敬浮屠、鑿井灌佛亦如之。

translations.literal: People are divided into five ranks, as in Cochin; their reverence for the Buddha, digging wells, and bathing the Buddha are likewise the same.
translations.idiomatic: Society was divided into five ranks, as in Cochin, and they showed the same devotion to Buddhism, digging wells, and bathing the Buddha image.

sentences.zh: 每旦，王及臣民取牛糞調水涂壁及地，又鍛為灰抹額及股，謂為敬佛。

translations.literal: Every morning the king and his subjects take cow dung mixed with water to smear walls and ground, and also burn it to ash to daub forehead and thighs, calling this reverence for the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Each dawn the king and people mixed cow dung with water to coat walls and floors, burned the rest to ash for their foreheads and thighs, and called this homage to the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 國中半崇回教，建禮拜寺數十處。

translations.literal: Half the country reveres Islam and has built several tens of mosques.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly half the population followed Islam and maintained several dozen mosques.

sentences.zh: 七日一禮，男女齋沐謝事。

translations.literal: Every seven days they perform worship; men and women bathe and abstain from affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped every seven days, when men and women bathed, fasted, and set aside worldly business.

sentences.zh: 午時拜天於寺，未時乃散。

translations.literal: At the noon hour they worship Heaven in the mosque; only at the wei hour do they disperse.
translations.idiomatic: At noon they prayed in the mosques and did not leave until the early afternoon.

sentences.zh: 王老不傳子而傳甥，無甥則傳弟，無弟則傳於國之有德者。

translations.literal: When the king grows old he does not pass the throne to a son but to a sister's son; if there is no sister's son, then to a younger brother; if no younger brother, then to one of merit in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Kings did not pass the throne to sons but to nephews; without a nephew it went to a younger brother, and without a brother to a worthy man of the realm.

sentences.zh: 國事皆決於二將領，以回回人為之。

translations.literal: All state affairs are decided by two generals, who are appointed from among the Hui people.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs were settled by two generals drawn from the Muslim community.

sentences.zh: 刑無鞭笞，輕者斷手足，重者罰金珠，尤重者夷族沒產。

translations.literal: In punishment there is no flogging; light offenses mean cutting off hands or feet, serious ones mean fines in gold and pearls, and the most serious mean exterminating the clan and confiscating property.
translations.idiomatic: There was no flogging: minor crimes cost a hand or foot, serious ones a fine in gold and pearls, and the gravest brought extinction of the clan and forfeiture of property.

sentences.zh: 鞫獄不承，則置其手指沸湯中，三日不爛即免罪。

translations.literal: In trying cases, if one does not confess, the fingers are placed in boiling water; if after three days they are not putrefied, guilt is remitted.
translations.idiomatic: If a prisoner denied guilt, his fingers were plunged into boiling water; if they had not rotted after three days he was acquitted.

sentences.zh: 免罪者，將領導以鼓樂，送還家，親戚致賀。

translations.literal: Those cleared of guilt are led home by the generals with drums and music, and relatives offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The acquitted were escorted home with drums and music by the generals, and kin came to congratulate them.

sentences.zh: 富家多植椰子樹至數千。

translations.literal: Wealthy households often plant coconut trees by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families might plant thousands of coconut palms.

sentences.zh: 其嫩者漿可飲，亦可釀酒，老者可作油、糖，亦可作飯。

translations.literal: The tender ones yield sap that can be drunk or made into wine; the old ones yield oil and sugar and can also serve as food.
translations.idiomatic: Young nuts gave drinkable sap and wine, while mature ones yielded oil, sugar, and a staple food.

sentences.zh: 干可構屋，葉可代瓦，殼可制杯，穰可索綯，鍛為灰可鑲金。

translations.literal: The trunk can build houses, the leaves can replace tiles, the shell can make cups, the husk can be twisted into rope, and ash from burning can inlay gold.
translations.idiomatic: Trunks served for timber, leaves for roofing, shells for cups, husks for cordage, and the ash for gold inlay work.

sentences.zh: 其他蔬果、畜產，多類中國。

translations.literal: Other fruits, vegetables, and livestock products mostly resemble those of China.
translations.idiomatic: Other produce and livestock largely resembled those found in China.

sentences.zh: 所貢物有寶石、珊瑚珠、琉璃瓶、琉璃枕、寶鐵刀、拂郎雙刃刀、金系腰、阿思模達涂兒氣、龍涎香、蘇合油、花氈單、伯蘭布、苾布之屬。

translations.literal: Tribute goods included precious stones, coral beads, glass bottles, glass pillows, precious iron knives, Frankish double-edged knives, gold belts, asafetida, ambergris, storax oil, flowered felt rugs, Persian cloth, bhuti cloth, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute included gems, coral beads, glass bottles and pillows, fine steel knives, Frankish double-edged blades, gold belts, asafetida, ambergris, storax, flowered felts, Persian textiles, bhuti cloth, and similar goods.

sentences.zh: 柯枝，或言即古盤盤國。

translations.literal: Cochin—some say it is the ancient state of Panpan.
translations.idiomatic: Cochin, said by some to be the ancient realm of Panpan.

sentences.zh: 宋、梁、隋、唐皆入貢。

translations.literal: Under Song, Liang, Sui, and Tang it all presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: It sent tribute in the Song, Liang, Sui, and Tang dynasties.

sentences.zh: 自小葛蘭西北行，順風一日夜可至。

translations.literal: Sailing northwest from Little Kulam, with a fair wind one can reach it in one day and night.
translations.idiomatic: From Little Kulam a fair wind carried one northwest to it in a day and a night.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，遣中官尹慶齎詔撫諭其國，賜以銷金帳幔、織金文綺、彩帛及華蓋。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the emperor sent the eunuch Yin Qing bearing an edict to console and instruct the country, bestowing gold-inlaid tent curtains, woven gold brocades, colored silks, and ceremonial canopies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 (1403) the eunuch Yin Qing carried an edict of reassurance and gifts of gold-inlaid hangings, brocades, silks, and state umbrellas.

sentences.zh: 六年覆命鄭和使其國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again ordered to send Zheng He on a mission to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zheng He was again dispatched to the realm.

sentences.zh: 九年，王可亦裡遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year King Keyili sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year King Keyili sent a tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 十年，鄭和再使其國，連二歲入貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zheng He again went on mission to their country, and tribute came two years in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zheng He visited again, and tribute arrived two years running.

sentences.zh: 其使者請賜印誥，封其國中之山。

translations.literal: Its envoys requested the grant of a seal and patent and the enfeoffment of a mountain within their country.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys asked for a seal and patent and for a mountain in their land to be enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 帝遣鄭和齎印賜其王，因撰碑文，命勒石山上。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Zheng He bearing the seal to invest their king, and composed an inscription, ordering it carved on stone on the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zheng He with the seal to invest the king, composed an inscription, and ordered it cut into the mountain stone.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：王化與天地流通，凡覆載之內、舉納於甄陶者，體造化之仁也。

translations.literal: The text reads: Royal transformation flows with Heaven and Earth; all within what covers and bears, brought into the potter's shaping, embodies the benevolence of creation and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: It read: Imperial civilizing power moves with Heaven and Earth; all that heaven covers and earth bears, shaped in the cosmic kiln, partakes of creative benevolence.

sentences.zh: 蓋天下無二理，生民無二心，憂戚喜樂之同情，安逸飽暖之同欲，奚有間於遐邇哉。

translations.literal: Surely under Heaven there is no second principle and among the living people no second heart; sorrow and joy share the same feeling, ease and fullness the same desire—how could there be division between far and near?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven admits but one principle and mankind but one heart; grief and joy, comfort and sufficiency are felt alike—what gap could there be between the near and the far?

sentences.zh: 任君民之寄者，當盡子民之道。

translations.literal: Who bears the charge of ruler and people ought to fulfill the way of parent to children.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever holds the trust of ruler and ruled must fulfill the duty of a father to his people.

sentences.zh: 《詩》雲「邦畿千里，惟民所止，肇域彼四海」。

translations.literal: The Odes say, 'The royal domain extends a thousand li—where the people dwell—and begins to mark off the four seas.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: 'The royal domain stretches a thousand li where the people rest, and begins to bound the four seas.'

sentences.zh: 《書》雲「東漸於海，西被於流沙，朔南暨聲教，訖於四海。」

translations.literal: The Documents say, 'Eastward it reaches the sea, westward it spreads to the drifting sands; north and south it attains to civilizing instruction, extending to the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: 'Eastward it reaches the sea, westward to the drifting sands; north and south its transforming voice extends to the four seas.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨天下，撫治華夷，一視同仁，無間彼此。

translations.literal: I rule all under Heaven, comforting and governing Chinese and barbarian alike, treating all with the same benevolence, without distinction between this side and that.'
translations.idiomatic: I rule the realm, governing Chinese and foreign peoples alike, with one benevolence for all and no division between near and far.'

sentences.zh: 推古聖帝明王之道，以合乎天地之心。

translations.literal: I extend the way of the ancient sage emperors and enlightened kings to accord with the heart of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: I extend the way of the ancient sage kings to align with the mind of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 遠邦異域，咸使各得其所，聞風向化者，爭恐後也。

translations.literal: Distant states and strange lands are all enabled to find their proper places; those who hear the wind and turn to transformation vie lest they be last.
translations.idiomatic: Distant realms are each settled in their place, and those who hear our transforming influence hurry to follow, fearing to lag behind.

sentences.zh: 柯枝國遠在西南，距海之濱，出諸蕃國之外，慕中華而歆德化久矣。

translations.literal: The state of Cochin lies far in the southwest on the edge of the sea, beyond the various fan states, and has long admired the Central Kingdom and delighted in its civilizing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Cochin lies far to the southwest on the seaboard, beyond the other maritime states, and has long yearned for China and its civilizing power.

sentences.zh: 命令之至，拳跽鼓舞，順附如歸，咸仰天而拜曰：「何幸中國聖人之教，沾及於我！」

translations.literal: When the command arrived, they knelt with fists raised and danced for joy, submitting as if returning home, all bowing toward Heaven and saying: 'How fortunate that the teaching of China's sages has reached even us!
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial command arrived they knelt and rejoiced, submitting as though coming home, and all bowed toward Heaven crying: 'How blessed we are that the teaching of China's sages has reached us!

sentences.zh: 乃數歲以來，國內豐穰，居有室廬，食飽魚鱉，衣足布帛，老者慈幼，少者敬長，熙熙然而樂，凌厲爭競之習無有也。

translations.literal: For several years now within the country there has been abundant harvest; people have houses to dwell in, eat their fill of fish and turtle, have enough cloth and silk for clothing; the old are kind to the young, the young respect the elders; all live in harmonious joy, and the harsh habits of fierce competition are gone.'
translations.idiomatic: For years the realm has been abundant: people have homes, full meals of fish and turtle, ample cloth and silk; the old cherish the young and the young honor their elders; life is serene, and the old fierce rivalries have vanished.'

sentences.zh: 山無猛獸，溪絕惡魚，海出奇珍，林產嘉木，諸物繁盛，倍越尋常。

translations.literal: In the mountains there are no fierce beasts; in the streams no evil fish; the sea yields strange treasures and the forests fine timber; all things flourish beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The hills hold no savage beasts, the streams no poisonous fish; the sea yields rare treasures and the forests fine timber; every bounty exceeds the common measure.

sentences.zh: 暴風不興，疾雨不作，札沴殄息，靡有害菑。

translations.literal: Violent winds do not arise, sudden rains do not fall, pestilence is extinguished, and there is no harmful calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Violent winds and sudden rains do not come; pestilence has ceased and no calamity harms the land.

sentences.zh: 蓋甚盛矣。

translations.literal: Truly it is most flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Surely prosperity has reached its height.

sentences.zh: 朕揆德薄，何能如是，非其長民者之所致歟？

translations.literal: I measure my virtue as slight—how could it be thus? Is it not owing to those who lead the people?
translations.idiomatic: My own virtue is slight; how could this be unless it came from those who govern the people?

sentences.zh: 乃封可亦裡為國王，賜以印章，俾撫治其民。

translations.literal: Therefore Keyili was enfeoffed as king and given a seal and patent, that he might comfort and rule his people.
translations.idiomatic: Keyili was therefore invested as king, granted a seal, and charged to govern his people.

sentences.zh: 並封其國中之山為鎮國之山，勒碑其上，垂示無窮。

translations.literal: A mountain within their country was also enfeoffed as the mountain that guards the state, and a stele was carved upon it to display this for endless generations.
translations.idiomatic: A mountain in the realm was enfeoffed as the state-protecting peak, with an inscription carved there to endure forever.

sentences.zh: 而系以銘曰：「截彼高山，作鎮海邦，吐煙出雲，為下國洪龐。

translations.literal: An epigraph was appended, saying: 'Cut down that high mountain to be guardian of the maritime state; it breathes forth mist and sends out clouds, a vast blessing to the lower realm.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription read: 'Hew that lofty peak to guard the seaboard state; breathing mist and sending forth clouds, a mighty blessing to the land below.

sentences.zh: 肅其煩高，時其雨暘，祛彼氛妖，作彼豐穰。

translations.literal: Subdue its vexing vapors and lofty tumult, time its rain and sunshine, dispel those miasmic demons, and make that abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Temper its storms and lofty airs, balance rain and fair weather, banish harmful mists, and bring forth rich harvests.

sentences.zh: 靡菑靡沴，永庇斯疆，優遊卒歲，室家胥慶。

translations.literal: Without calamity or pestilence, forever sheltering this borderland; at ease through the year's end, every household rejoicing together.
translations.idiomatic: Free of disaster and plague, ever sheltering this realm; at peace through the year, every household sharing its joy.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ah!

sentences.zh: 山之嶄兮，海之深矣，勒此銘詩，相為終始。」

translations.literal: Lofty the mountain, deep the sea—this inscribed verse is carved to mark beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty the mountain, deep the sea—this verse is carved to stand from first to last.

sentences.zh: 自後，間歲入貢。

translations.literal: From then on tribute came in alternate years.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute arrived in alternate years.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，復遣鄭和撫諭其國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande Zheng He was again sent to console and instruct their country.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He was again dispatched to reassure the realm.

sentences.zh: 八年，王可亦裡遣使偕錫蘭山諸國來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year King Keyili sent envoys together with Ceylon and other states to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year King Keyili sent envoys with Ceylon and other states on a tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，遣其使者附爪哇貢舶還國，並賜敕勞王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong its envoys were sent home on Java's tribute vessel, and an imperial letter was bestowed to console the king.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 (1436) its envoys were sent home on Java's tribute ship, and an imperial letter of praise was granted to the king.

sentences.zh: 王，瑣裡人，崇釋教。

translations.literal: The king is a Suoli person and reveres the Buddhist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The king is of the Suoli people and follows Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 佛座四旁皆水溝，復穿一井。

translations.literal: On all four sides of the Buddha's seat are water channels, and a well is also dug.
translations.idiomatic: Water channels surround the Buddha's seat on four sides, and a well is dug nearby.

sentences.zh: 每旦鳴鐘鼓，汲水灌佛，三浴之，始羅拜而退。

translations.literal: Every morning bells and drums are sounded; water is drawn to bathe the Buddha three times, and only then do they spread their robes, bow, and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Each dawn bells and drums sound; water is drawn to bathe the image three times before worshippers bow and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 其國與錫蘭山對峙，中通古裡，東界大山，三面距海。

translations.literal: Its country faces Ceylon across the sea; in the center it connects with Guli; to the east it borders great mountains; on three sides it is bounded by the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The realm faces Ceylon across the water, links inland to Calicut, borders great mountains to the east, and is surrounded by sea on three sides.

sentences.zh: 俗頗淳。

translations.literal: Its customs are rather pure.
translations.idiomatic: Customs are comparatively upright.

sentences.zh: 築室，以椰子樹為材，取葉為苫以覆屋，風雨皆可蔽。

translations.literal: In building houses they use coconut trees as timber and take the leaves as thatch to cover the roof, so that wind and rain are both kept out.
translations.idiomatic: Houses are built of coconut timber with leaf thatch for roofing, giving shelter from wind and rain alike.

sentences.zh: 人分五等：一曰南昆，王族類；

translations.literal: People are divided into five ranks: first, Nankun, of the royal clan;
translations.idiomatic: Society was divided into five ranks: first, the Nankun, of the royal line;

sentences.zh: 二曰回回，三曰哲地，皆富民；

translations.literal: second, Huihui; third, Zhedi—all wealthy people;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Hui Muslims; third, the Zhedi—all wealthy classes;

sentences.zh: 四曰革全，皆牙儈；

translations.literal: fourth, Gequan—all brokers;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the Gequan—all brokers;

sentences.zh: 五曰木瓜。

translations.literal: fifth, Mugua.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the Mugua.

sentences.zh: 木瓜最貧，為人執賤役者。

translations.literal: The Mugua are poorest and perform menial service for others.
translations.idiomatic: The Mugua were the poorest and performed menial labor for others.

sentences.zh: 屋高不得過三尺。

translations.literal: Their houses may be no more than three chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Their dwellings could be no more than three feet high.

sentences.zh: 衣上不得過臍，下不得過膝。

translations.literal: Their clothing above may not pass the navel, nor below the knee.
translations.idiomatic: Their garments could not rise above the navel or fall below the knee.

sentences.zh: 途遇南昆、哲地人，輒伏地，俟其過乃起。

translations.literal: Meeting Nankun or Zhedi people on the road, they at once prostrate themselves and do not rise until the others have passed.
translations.idiomatic: On meeting a Nankun or Zhedi they had to prostrate themselves in the road and not rise until the other had passed.

sentences.zh: 氣候常熱。

translations.literal: The climate is constantly hot.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is perpetually hot.

sentences.zh: 一歲中，二三月時有少雨，國人皆治舍儲食物以俟。

translations.literal: Within a year, in the second and third months there is a little rain; the people all repair their houses and store food in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second and third months there is a brief rainy season, when everyone repairs their homes and lays in stores of food.

sentences.zh: 五六月間大雨不止，街市成河，七月始晴，八月後不復雨，歲歲皆然。

translations.literal: From the fifth to the sixth month great rain does not cease; streets and markets become rivers; only in the seventh month does it clear; after the eighth month rain does not come again—thus every year.
translations.idiomatic: From the fifth through the sixth month monsoon rains turn the streets into rivers; skies clear in the seventh month, and after the eighth month the rains cease—the same cycle every year.

sentences.zh: 田瘠少收，諸谷皆產，獨無麥。

translations.literal: Fields are poor and yields small; all grains are produced, but wheat alone is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Fields are lean and yields modest; every grain grows except wheat.

sentences.zh: 諸畜亦皆有，獨無鵝與驢雲。

translations.literal: All livestock are also present, but geese and donkeys alone are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: All common livestock are found there, but not geese or donkeys.

sentences.zh: 小葛蘭 大葛蘭

translations.literal: Little Kulam; Great Kulam
translations.idiomatic: These are Little Kulam and Great Kulam

sentences.zh: 小葛蘭，其國與柯枝接境。

translations.literal: Little Kulam—its country borders Cochin.
translations.idiomatic: Little Kulam bordered Cochin.

sentences.zh: 自錫蘭山西北行六晝夜可達。

translations.literal: Sailing northwest from Ceylon, one can reach it in six days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Six days' sail northwest from Ceylon brought one there.

sentences.zh: 東大山，西大海，南北地窄，西洋小國也。

translations.literal: To the east are great mountains, to the west the great sea; north and south the land is narrow—it is a small state of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Great mountains lay to the east and the open sea to the west; the land was narrow north and south—a small state of the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年遣使附古裡、蘇門答剌入貢，賜其王錦綺、紗羅、鞍馬諸物，其使者亦有賜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongle envoys were sent attached to Guli and Samudra to present tribute; the king was bestowed brocades, gauzes, saddles, horses, and other things, and the envoys also received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 5 (1407) envoys joined Calicut and Samudra on a tribute mission; the king received brocades, gauzes, saddles, horses, and other gifts, and the envoys were rewarded as well.

sentences.zh: 王及群下皆瑣裡人，奉釋教。

translations.literal: The king and all his followers are Suoli people and observe the Buddhist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The king and his people were Suoli and followed Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 重牛及他婚喪諸禮，多與錫蘭同。

translations.literal: Their reverence for cattle and other rites of marriage and mourning mostly resemble those of Ceylon.
translations.idiomatic: Their veneration of cattle and their wedding and funeral customs largely matched those of Ceylon.

sentences.zh: 俗淳。

translations.literal: Customs are pure.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were upright.

sentences.zh: 土薄，收穫少，仰給榜葛剌。

translations.literal: The soil is thin and harvests small; they rely on Bengal for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was poor and yields modest; the realm depended on Bengal for grain.

sentences.zh: 鄭和嘗使其國。

translations.literal: Zheng He once sent a mission to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He had visited the realm on mission.

sentences.zh: 厥貢惟珍珠傘、白棉布、胡椒。

translations.literal: Their tribute consisted only of pearl umbrellas, white cotton cloth, and pepper.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute consisted of pearl umbrellas, white cotton cloth, and pepper.

sentences.zh: 又有大葛蘭者，波濤湍悍，舟不可泊，故商人罕至。

translations.literal: There is also Great Kulam, where waves and currents are violent and boats cannot anchor, so merchants rarely come.
translations.idiomatic: Great Kulam had fierce seas where ships could not anchor, so merchants seldom called.

sentences.zh: 土黑墳，本宜穀麥，民懶事耕作，歲賴烏爹之米以足食。

translations.literal: The soil is black and fertile and suited to grain and wheat, but the people are lazy about farming and each year rely on rice from Udai to fill their food needs.
translations.idiomatic: The black fertile soil could bear grain and wheat, but the people were slack farmers and each year lived on rice shipped from Udai.

sentences.zh: 風俗、物產，多類小葛蘭。

translations.literal: Customs and products mostly resemble those of Little Kulam.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and products largely resembled those of Little Kulam.

sentences.zh: 錫蘭山

translations.literal: Ceylon
translations.idiomatic: Ceylon

sentences.zh: 錫蘭山，或云即古狼牙修。

translations.literal: Ceylon—some say it is the ancient state of Langyaxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ceylon, identified by some with the ancient realm of Langyaxiu.

sentences.zh: 梁時曾通中國。

translations.literal: In the Liang dynasty it once communicated with China.
translations.idiomatic: It had contact with China as early as the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 自蘇門答剌順風十二晝夜可達。

translations.literal: From Samudra, with a fair wind, one can reach it in twelve days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve days' sail with a fair wind from Samudra brought one there.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，鄭和使西洋至其地，其王亞烈苦奈兒欲害和，和覺，去之他國。

translations.literal: During Yongle, when Zheng He went on mission to the Western Ocean and reached their land, King Yalie Kunai'er wished to harm He; He perceived this and left for another country.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign Zheng He reached the island on a Western Ocean mission; King Yalie Kunai'er plotted against him, but He sensed danger and sailed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 王又不睦鄰境，屢邀劫往來使臣，諸蕃皆苦之。

translations.literal: The king was also at odds with neighboring lands and repeatedly waylaid traveling envoys; all the fan states suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: The king also feuded with neighbors and repeatedly robbed passing envoys, to the distress of every maritime state.

sentences.zh: 及和歸，復經其地，乃誘和至國中，發兵五萬劫和，塞歸路。

translations.literal: When He returned and again passed their land, he was lured into the country; fifty thousand troops were raised to rob He and block the homeward route.
translations.idiomatic: On his return voyage He passed the island again; the king lured him ashore, sent fifty thousand men to attack him, and cut off his retreat.

sentences.zh: 和乃率步卒二千，由間道乘虛攻拔其城，生擒亞烈苦奈兒及妻子、頭目，獻俘於朝。

translations.literal: He then led two thousand foot soldiers by a bypath, struck when they were exposed, stormed and took their city, captured Yalie Kunai'er alive together with wife, children, and chiefs, and presented the captives at court.
translations.idiomatic: He led two thousand infantry by a hidden route, took the city by surprise, captured Yalie Kunai'er with his family and chiefs, and sent them to the court as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 廷臣請行戮，帝憫其無知，並妻子皆釋，且給以衣食。

translations.literal: Court officials requested execution, but the emperor pitied their ignorance; wife and children were all released and given food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers urged execution, but the emperor pitied their ignorance, freed the king and his family, and provided food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 命擇其族之賢者立之。

translations.literal: He ordered that a worthy man of their clan be chosen and established as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a worthy member of the royal clan to be chosen and enthroned.

sentences.zh: 有邪把乃那者，諸俘囚咸稱其賢，乃遣使齎印誥，封為王，其舊王亦遣歸。

translations.literal: There was one Xiebanaina; all the captives praised his worth, so envoys were sent bearing seal and patent to enfeoff him as king, and the former king was also sent home.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Xiebanaina was praised by all the captives as worthy; envoys invested him with seal and patent as king, and the deposed ruler was sent home.

sentences.zh: 自是海外諸蕃益服天子威德，貢使載道，王遂屢入貢。

translations.literal: From then on the various fan states beyond the sea increasingly submitted to the Son of Heaven's majesty and virtue; tribute envoys filled the roads, and the king thereafter repeatedly presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the maritime states submitted ever more to imperial majesty; tribute missions crowded the routes, and the king sent repeated embassies.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，鄭和撫諭其國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande Zheng He was sent to console and instruct their country.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He was dispatched to reassure the realm.

sentences.zh: 八年，王不剌葛麻巴忽剌批遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year King Bulagemabahulapi sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year King Bulagemabahulapi sent a tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 正統元年命附爪哇貢舶歸，賜敕諭之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong they were ordered to return on Java's tribute vessel, and an imperial letter of instruction was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 (1436) they were sent home on Java's tribute ship with an imperial letter of guidance.

sentences.zh: 十年偕滿剌加使者來貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year envoys came together with those from Malacca to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year envoys arrived with those from Malacca on a tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 天順三年，王葛力生夏剌昔利把交剌惹遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshun King Gelishengxialixibajiaolara sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 3 (1459) King Gelishengxialixibajiaolara sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 嗣後不復至。

translations.literal: After that they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: No further missions followed.

sentences.zh: 其國，地廣人稠，貨物多聚，亞於爪哇。

translations.literal: Its country is broad in territory and dense in population; goods gather in abundance, second only to Java.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was broad and populous, with goods gathered in quantity rivaled only by Java.

sentences.zh: 東南海中有山三四座，總名曰翠藍嶼。

translations.literal: In the southeast sea there are three or four mountains, collectively called the Emerald Isles.
translations.idiomatic: Three or four isles in the southeastern sea were together called the Emerald Isles.

sentences.zh: 大小七門，門皆可通舟。

translations.literal: There are seven gates large and small, and every gate admits boats.
translations.idiomatic: Seven channels, large and small, all allowed passage for boats.

sentences.zh: 中一山尤高大，番名梭篤蠻山。

translations.literal: One mountain in the midst is especially lofty; in the fan tongue it is called Mount Suoduman.
translations.idiomatic: One peak in their midst was especially tall, known locally as Mount Suoduman.

sentences.zh: 其人皆巢居穴處，赤身髡發。

translations.literal: Its people all nest in trees and dwell in caves, going naked with shaved heads.
translations.idiomatic: The inhabitants lived in tree nests and caves, naked and with shaven heads.

sentences.zh: 相傳釋迦佛昔經此山，浴於水，或竊其袈裟，佛誓云：「後有穿衣者，必爛其皮肉。」

translations.literal: Tradition says that in former times Shakyamuni Buddha passed this mountain and bathed in the water; someone stole his kasaya robe, and the Buddha swore: 'Hereafter whoever wears clothes shall have flesh and skin putrefy.
translations.idiomatic: Legend held that Shakyamuni once passed the mountain and bathed there; when someone stole his robe, the Buddha vowed: 'Whoever wears clothes hereafter shall have his flesh rot away.

sentences.zh: 自是，寸布掛身輒發瘡毒，故男女皆裸體。

translations.literal: From then on, if even an inch of cloth touched the body sores and poison broke out, so men and women are all naked.'
translations.idiomatic: After that even a scrap of cloth on the skin brought sores and poison, so men and women went entirely naked.'

sentences.zh: 但紉木葉蔽其前後，或圍以布，故又名裸形國。

translations.literal: They only string tree leaves to cover front and back, or wrap with cloth, and therefore it is also called the Land of Naked Forms.
translations.idiomatic: They wore only leaves strung before and behind, or sometimes a cloth wrap, and the land was also called the Realm of Naked Forms.

sentences.zh: 地不生谷，惟啖魚蝦及山芋、波羅密、芭蕉實之屬。

translations.literal: The land does not produce grain; they eat only fish, shrimp, taro, jackfruit, plantains, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Grain did not grow there; the people lived on fish, shrimp, taro, jackfruit, plantains, and similar foods.

sentences.zh: 自此山西行七日，見鸚哥嘴山。

translations.literal: Sailing west from this mountain for seven days, one sees Parrot-Beak Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days' sail west from the isle brought one to Parrot-Beak Mountain.

sentences.zh: 又二三日抵佛堂山，即入錫蘭國境。

translations.literal: After two or three more days one reaches Buddha-Hall Mountain, and there one enters the territory of Ceylon.
translations.idiomatic: Two or three days farther brought one to Buddha-Hall Mountain and the border of Ceylon.

sentences.zh: 海邊山石上有一足跡，長三尺許。

translations.literal: On a rock by the seashore there is a footprint about three chi long.
translations.idiomatic: On a seaside rock there was a footprint some three feet long.

sentences.zh: 故老雲，佛從翠藍嶼來，踐此，故足跡尚存。

translations.literal: The elders say the Buddha came from the Emerald Isles, trod here, and therefore the footprint remains.
translations.idiomatic: Elders said the Buddha came from the Emerald Isles, stepped here, and left the print.

sentences.zh: 中有淺水，四時不乾，人皆手蘸拭目洗面，曰「佛水清淨」。

translations.literal: Within it is shallow water that never dries in any season; people all dip with their hands to wipe their eyes and wash their faces, calling it 'the Buddha's pure water.'
translations.idiomatic: Shallow water there never dried; people dipped their hands to wash eyes and face, calling it the Buddha's pure water.

sentences.zh: 山下僧寺有釋迦真身，側臥床上。

translations.literal: In a monk's temple below the mountain is the true body of Shakyamuni, reclining on its side upon a couch.
translations.idiomatic: In a monastery below lay the true body of Shakyamuni, reclining on a couch.

sentences.zh: 旁有佛牙及舍利，相傳佛涅槃處也。

translations.literal: Beside it are the Buddha's tooth and relics; tradition says this is where the Buddha entered nirvana.
translations.idiomatic: Beside it were the Buddha's tooth and relics at the place where he was said to have entered nirvana.

sentences.zh: 其寢座以沉香為之，飾以諸色寶石，莊嚴甚。

translations.literal: His couch is made of agarwood and adorned with gems of every color, most splendid.
translations.idiomatic: The couch was of agarwood set with gems of every hue, splendidly adorned.

sentences.zh: 王所居側有大山，高出雲漢。

translations.literal: Beside where the king dwells is a great mountain rising above the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Beside the royal residence stood a great mountain towering into the clouds.

sentences.zh: 其顛有巨人足跡，入石深二尺，長八尺餘，雲是盤古遺蹟。

translations.literal: On its summit is a giant's footprint, sunk two chi into the stone and more than eight chi long; it is said to be a trace left by Pangu.
translations.idiomatic: On the summit was a giant footprint two feet deep in the rock and more than eight feet long, said to be a relic of Pangu.

sentences.zh: 此山產紅雅姑、青雅姑、黃雅姑、昔剌泥、窟沒藍等諸色寶石。

translations.literal: This mountain produces red yagu, blue yagu, yellow yagu, sirani, and gululan, gems of every color.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain yielded red, blue, and yellow yagu, sirani, gululan, and other colored gems.

sentences.zh: 每大雨，沖流山下，土人競拾之。

translations.literal: Whenever great rain falls, they are washed down the mountain and the natives compete to gather them.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains washed gems down the slopes for the people to gather.

sentences.zh: 海旁有浮沙，珠蚌聚其內，光彩瀲灩。

translations.literal: By the sea is drifting sand within which pearl oysters gather, their luster shimmering.
translations.idiomatic: Drifting sand by the shore held pearl oysters of shimmering luster.

sentences.zh: 王使人撈取，置之地，蚌爛而取其珠，故其國珠寶特富。

translations.literal: The king sends men to dredge them up and set them on land; when the shells rot the pearls are taken, and therefore the country's gems and pearls are especially rich.
translations.idiomatic: The king had men dredge the oysters ashore; when the shells rotted the pearls were taken, making the realm especially rich in gems.

sentences.zh: 王，瑣裡國人。

translations.literal: The king is a man of the state of Suoli.
translations.idiomatic: The king was a native of Suoli.

sentences.zh: 崇釋教，重牛，日取牛糞燒灰涂其體，又調以水，遍塗地上，乃禮佛。

translations.literal: He reveres the Buddhist teaching and esteems cattle; daily he takes cow dung, burns it to ash to smear his body, mixes it with water, and spreads it over the ground before worshipping the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Buddhism and revered cattle; each day he burned cow dung to ash for his body, mixed the ash with water to coat the ground, and then worshipped the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 手足直舒，腹貼於地以為敬，王及庶民皆如之。

translations.literal: Hands and feet are stretched straight and the belly pressed to the ground as reverence; king and common people are all alike.
translations.idiomatic: King and people alike prostrated with limbs extended and belly to the earth.

sentences.zh: 不食牛肉，止食其乳，死則瘞之，有殺牛者，罪至死。

translations.literal: They do not eat beef, only drink its milk; when cattle die they are buried, and whoever kills a cow is punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: They did not eat beef, only drank milk; dead cattle were buried, and killing a cow was a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 氣候常熱，米粟豐足，民富饒，然不喜啖飯。

translations.literal: The climate is constantly hot; rice and grain are abundant and the people wealthy, yet they do not like to eat cooked rice.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was perpetually hot, grain plentiful, and the people prosperous, yet they disliked eating rice openly.

sentences.zh: 欲啖，則於暗處，不令人見。

translations.literal: When they wish to eat, they do so in a dark place where others cannot see.
translations.idiomatic: When they ate rice they did so in private, out of sight.

sentences.zh: 遍體皆毫毛，悉薙去，惟發不薙。

translations.literal: Hair covers the whole body and is all shaved off, only the hair on the head is not shaved.
translations.idiomatic: Body hair was shaved away, but the hair of the head was left.

sentences.zh: 所貢物有珠、珊瑚、寶石、水晶、撒哈剌、西洋布、乳香、木香、樹香、檀香、沒藥、硫黃、藤竭、蘆薈、烏木、胡椒、碗石、馴象之屬。

translations.literal: Tribute goods include pearls, coral, gems, crystal, sahala cloth, Western Ocean cloth, frankincense, costus, tree resin, sandalwood, myrrh, sulfur, gamboge, aloe, ebony, pepper, bowl-stone, tame elephants, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute included pearls, coral, gems, crystal, sahala and Western cloth, frankincense, costus, aromatic woods, sandalwood, myrrh, sulfur, gamboge, aloe, ebony, pepper, bowl-stone, tame elephants, and similar goods.

sentences.zh: 榜葛剌

translations.literal: Bengal
translations.idiomatic: Bengal

sentences.zh: 榜葛剌，即漢身毒國，東漢曰天竺。

translations.literal: Bengal is the Shendu country of Han; in Eastern Han it was called Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Bengal was the Shendu realm of Han times, called Tianzhu in the Eastern Han.

sentences.zh: 其後中天竺貢於梁，南天竺貢於魏。

translations.literal: Later Central Tianzhu presented tribute to Liang and Southern Tianzhu to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later Central India sent tribute to the Liang and Southern India to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 唐亦分五天竺，又名五印度。

translations.literal: Tang also divided it into the Five Tianzhu, also called the Five Indias.
translations.idiomatic: Tang likewise spoke of the Five Indias.

sentences.zh: 宋仍名天竺。

translations.literal: Song still called it Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Song sources still used the name Tianzhu.

sentences.zh: 榜葛剌則東印度也。

translations.literal: Bengal is Eastern India.
translations.idiomatic: Bengal was Eastern India.

sentences.zh: 自蘇門答剌順風二十晝夜可至。

translations.literal: From Samudra, with a fair wind, one can reach it in twenty days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days' sail with a fair wind from Samudra brought one there.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年，其王靄牙思丁遣使來朝，貢方物，宴賚有差。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle its king Saiyasiding sent envoys to court, presenting local products; feasts and gifts were graded accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 6 (1408) King Saiyasiding sent envoys to court with regional tribute and was entertained and rewarded in due measure.

sentences.zh: 七年，其使凡再至，攜從者二百三十餘人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year its envoys came twice in all, bringing more than two hundred thirty attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year envoys came twice, with more than two hundred thirty followers.

sentences.zh: 帝方招徠絕域，頒賜甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor was then summoning distant realms and bestowed gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was courting distant realms and gave lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 自是比年入貢。

translations.literal: From then on tribute came every year.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute then arrived yearly.

sentences.zh: 十年，貢使將至，遣官宴之於鎮江。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, as tribute envoys were about to arrive, officials were sent to feast them at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year officials were sent to entertain the approaching envoys at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 既將事，使者告其王之喪。

translations.literal: When the business was nearly concluded, the envoys announced their king's death.
translations.idiomatic: As the audience drew near, the envoys reported their king's death.

sentences.zh: 遣官往祭，封嗣子賽勿丁為王。

translations.literal: Officials were sent to perform the mourning rites and the heir Saiwuding was enfeoffed as king.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to perform the mourning rites and invest the heir Saiwuding as king.

sentences.zh: 十二年，嗣王遣使奉表來謝，貢麒麟及名馬方物。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the succeeding king sent envoys with a memorial of thanks, presenting a qilin and famous horses among local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the new king sent envoys with a memorial of thanks, offering a qilin, fine horses, and other tribute.

sentences.zh: 禮官請表賀，帝勿許。

translations.literal: Ritual officials requested a congratulatory memorial; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials proposed a congratulatory memorial, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 明年遣侯顯齎詔使其國，王與妃、大臣皆有賜。

translations.literal: The next year Hou Xian was sent bearing an edict on mission to their country; the king, consort, and ministers all received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Hou Xian carried an edict to the realm; the king, queen, and ministers all received gifts.

sentences.zh: 正統三年貢麒麟，百官表賀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong a qilin was presented as tribute and all officials submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 3 (1438) a qilin was sent as tribute and the whole court offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 明年又入貢。

translations.literal: The next year tribute came again.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute came again the following year.

sentences.zh: 自是不復至。

translations.literal: From then on they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: No further missions followed.

sentences.zh: 其國，地大物阜。

translations.literal: Its country is broad in territory and rich in goods.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was vast and abundantly supplied.

sentences.zh: 城池街市，聚貨通商，繁華類中國。

translations.literal: Walled cities, streets, and markets gather goods and conduct trade, flourishing like China.
translations.idiomatic: Its walled cities and markets teemed with trade, flourishing like those of China.

sentences.zh: 四時氣候常如夏。

translations.literal: Through the four seasons the climate is always like summer.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was summer-like year round.

sentences.zh: 土沃，一歲二稔，不待耔耘。

translations.literal: The soil is fertile; there are two harvests in a year without need for transplanting or harrowing.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was rich and yielded two harvests a year without transplanting or heavy tillage.

sentences.zh: 俗淳龐，有文字，男女勤於耕織。

translations.literal: Customs are pure and simple; they have writing; men and women are diligent in farming and weaving.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were plain and honest; they had a written language, and men and women worked diligently at farming and weaving.

sentences.zh: 容體皆黑，間有白者。

translations.literal: Their bodies are all black, with occasionally white persons among them.
translations.idiomatic: The people were generally dark-skinned, though a few were fair.

sentences.zh: 王及官民皆回回人，喪祭冠婚，悉用其禮。

translations.literal: The king, officials, and people are all Hui Muslims; mourning, sacrifice, capping, and marriage all use their rites.
translations.idiomatic: The king, officials, and people were Muslims who followed Islamic rites for death, worship, coming of age, and marriage.

sentences.zh: 男子皆薙發，裹以白布。

translations.literal: Men all shave the head and wrap themselves in white cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Men shaved their heads and wrapped themselves in white cloth.

sentences.zh: 衣從頸貫下，用布圍之。

translations.literal: Clothing runs down from the neck and is wrapped with cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Garments hung from the neck and were wrapped about the body with cloth.

sentences.zh: 歷不置閏。

translations.literal: The calendar does not insert intercalary months.
translations.idiomatic: Their calendar had no intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 刑有笞杖徒流數等。

translations.literal: Punishments include beating with the rod, the cudgel, penal servitude, and exile, among several grades.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments ranged through beating, cudgeling, penal servitude, and exile.

sentences.zh: 官司上下，亦有行移。

translations.literal: Among offices high and low there are also written communications.
translations.idiomatic: Government offices exchanged written documents as in China.

sentences.zh: 醫卜、陰陽、百工、技藝悉如中國，蓋皆前世所流入也。

translations.literal: Medicine, divination, yin-yang arts, the hundred crafts, and skills are all like China's—presumably all introduced in earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine, divination, yin-yang lore, crafts, and arts all resembled China's, having been introduced in earlier times.

sentences.zh: 其王敬天朝。

translations.literal: Its king reveres the Celestial Court.
translations.idiomatic: The king held the Celestial Court in reverence.

sentences.zh: 聞使者至，遣官具儀物，以千騎來迎。

translations.literal: Hearing that envoys have arrived, he sends officials with ritual objects and comes to welcome them with a thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys arrived he sent officials with ceremonial gear and a thousand horsemen to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 王宮高廣，柱皆黃銅包飾，雕琢花獸。

translations.literal: The royal palace is lofty and broad; the pillars are all clad in yellow bronze with carved flowers and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: The palace was lofty and vast, its pillars sheathed in gilt bronze carved with flowers and beasts.

sentences.zh: 左右設長廊，內列明甲馬隊千餘，外列巨人，明盔甲，執刀劍弓矢，威儀甚壯。

translations.literal: Long corridors are set to left and right; within are arrayed more than a thousand armored cavalry in bright armor, and without stand giant men in bright helmets and armor holding swords, bows, and arrows—the guard display is very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Long corridors flanked the hall; within stood more than a thousand armored horsemen, and without giant guards in bright armor with sword, bow, and arrow—a formidable display.

sentences.zh: 丹墀左右，設孔雀翎傘蓋百餘，又置象隊百餘於殿前。

translations.literal: To left and right of the red steps are set more than a hundred parasols of peacock feathers, and more than a hundred elephants are stationed before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred peacock-feather parasols lined the court, with another hundred elephants before the hall.

sentences.zh: 王飾八寶冠，箕踞殿上高座，橫劍於膝。

translations.literal: The king wears a crown of the eight treasures, sits with legs spread on a high seat in the hall, and lays a sword across his knees.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a crown of eight treasures, sat with legs spread on a high throne, and rested a sword across his knees.

sentences.zh: 朝使入，令拄銀杖者二人來導，五步一呼，至中則止；

translations.literal: When the court envoy enters, two men bearing silver staffs are ordered to guide him, calling out every five paces and stopping at the center;
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy entered, two attendants with silver staffs led him forward, calling out every five paces and halting at the center;

sentences.zh: 又拄金杖者二人，導如初。

translations.literal: Again two men bearing gold staffs guide as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Two more attendants with gold staffs then led him forward in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 其王拜迎詔，叩頭，手加額。

translations.literal: Its king bows to welcome the edict, kowtows, and places his hands upon his forehead.
translations.idiomatic: The king bowed to receive the imperial edict, kowtowed, and pressed his hands to his forehead.

sentences.zh: 開讀受賜訖，設絨毯於殿，宴朝使；

translations.literal: After the edict is opened, read, and gifts received, a wool rug is spread in the hall and the court envoy is feasted;
translations.idiomatic: Once the edict had been read and the gifts accepted, a wool carpet was laid in the hall and a banquet was held for the envoy;

sentences.zh: 不飲酒，以薔薇露和香蜜水飲之。

translations.literal: They do not drink wine, but drink rose dew mixed with honeyed fragrant water.
translations.idiomatic: No wine was served; instead they drank rose water blended with honeyed perfumed water.

sentences.zh: 贈使者金盔、金繫腰、金瓶、金盆，其副則悉用銀，從者皆有贈。

translations.literal: They present the envoy with gold helmets, gold girdles, gold bottles, and gold basins; deputies all use silver, and attendants all receive gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was given gold helmets, gold belts, gold bottles, and gold basins; his deputies received silver equivalents, and every member of the retinue was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 厥貢：良馬、金銀琉璃器、青花白瓷、鶴頂、犀角、翠羽、鸚鵡、洗白苾布、兜鑼綿、撒哈剌、糖霜、乳香、熟香、烏香、麻藤香、烏爹泥、紫膠、藤竭、烏木、蘇木、胡椒、粗黃。

translations.literal: Their tribute: fine horses, gold and silver glassware, blue-and-white porcelain, casques, rhinoceros horn, kingfisher feathers, parrots, bleached cotton cloth, douluo cotton, sahala, sugar frost, frankincense, prepared incense, black incense, hemp-vine incense, uddamli, lac, rattan sap, ebony, sappanwood, pepper, and crude yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute included fine horses, gold and silver glassware, blue-and-white porcelain, hornbill casques, rhinoceros horn, kingfisher plumes, parrots, bleached cotton, douluo cotton, sahala cloth, sugar crystals, frankincense, prepared incense, black incense, hemp-vine incense, uddamli, lac, rattan gum, ebony, sappanwood, pepper, and orpiment.

sentences.zh: 沼納朴兒

translations.literal: Zhaonapu'er
translations.idiomatic: Ganenapuli

sentences.zh: 沼納朴兒，其國在榜葛剌之西。

translations.literal: Ganenapuli—its country lies to the west of Bengal.
translations.idiomatic: Ganenapuli lay west of Bengal.

sentences.zh: 或言即中印度，古所稱佛國也。

translations.literal: Some say it is Middle India, the Buddhist land spoken of in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Some identified it with Middle India, the Buddhist realm known to earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年遣使者齎敕撫諭其國，賜王亦不剌金絨錦、金織文綺、彩帛等物。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle an envoy was sent bearing an edict to console and instruct their country, bestowing upon King Yibulajin velvet brocade, gold-woven patterned silk, colored silks, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 10 (1412) an envoy carried an edict of reassurance to the realm and granted King Yibulajin velvet brocade, gold-woven silk, colored cloth, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 十八年，榜葛剌使者醞其國王數舉兵侵擾，詔中官侯顯齎敕諭以睦鄰保境之義，因賜之彩幣；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year a Bengal envoy accused its king of repeatedly raising troops to invade and harass; the emperor ordered the eunuch Hou Xian to carry an edict instructing him in the principle of neighborly friendship and guarding borders, and bestowed colored silks;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year a Bengal envoy complained that its king had repeatedly invaded and raided; the court sent the eunuch Hou Xian with an edict on good neighborly conduct and border peace, along with colored silks;

sentences.zh: 所過金剛寶座之地，亦有賜。

translations.literal: Where he passed the place of the Diamond Throne, there were also gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts were also bestowed at the Diamond Throne site through which he passed.

sentences.zh: 然其王以去中國絕遠，朝貢竟不至。

translations.literal: Yet its king, considering how utterly remote he was from China, never came to court with tribute after all.
translations.idiomatic: But the king, judging China impossibly distant, never sent tribute to court.

sentences.zh: 祖法兒

translations.literal: Zufar
translations.idiomatic: Dhofar

sentences.zh: 祖法兒，自古裡西北放舟，順風十晝夜可至。

translations.literal: Dhofar—from Calicut's northwest one puts out to sea, and with a fair wind can reach it in ten days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Dhofar lay northwest of Calicut; ten days' sail with a fair wind brought one there.

sentences.zh: 永樂十九年遣使偕阿丹、剌撒諸國入貢，命鄭和齎璽書賜物報之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yongle envoys came together with Aden, Las'a, and other states to present tribute; Zheng He was ordered to carry the imperial letter and gifts in response.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 19 (1421) envoys arrived with those from Aden, Las'a, and other states; Zheng He was dispatched with an imperial letter and return gifts.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，貢使復至。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year tribute envoys came again.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute envoys came again in the twenty-first year.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，和再使其國，其王阿里即遣使朝貢，八年達京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande He again sent a mission to their country; King Ali immediately dispatched envoys with tribute, reaching the capital in the eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He visited again; King Ali promptly sent tribute envoys who reached the capital in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 正統元年還國，賜璽書獎王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong they returned home, and an imperial letter was bestowed praising the king.
translations.idiomatic: They returned home in Zhengtong 1 (1436), and the king received an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 其國東南大海，西北重山，天時常若八九月。

translations.literal: Its country has the great sea to the southeast and layered mountains to the northwest; the weather is always like the eighth or ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: The realm faced the open sea to the southeast and rugged mountains to the northwest, with weather perpetually like late summer or early autumn.

sentences.zh: 五穀、蔬果、諸畜咸備。

translations.literal: The five grains, fruits, vegetables, and all kinds of livestock are all complete.
translations.idiomatic: Grain, fruit, vegetables, and livestock were all abundant.

sentences.zh: 人體頎碩。

translations.literal: People's bodies are tall and large.
translations.idiomatic: The people were tall and strongly built.

sentences.zh: 王及臣民悉奉回回教，婚喪亦遵其制。

translations.literal: The king and officials and people all follow the Hui Muslim religion; marriage and mourning also follow its regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The king and his subjects were Muslims who observed Islamic rites for marriage and mourning.

sentences.zh: 多建禮拜寺。

translations.literal: Many mosques are built.
translations.idiomatic: Mosques were built throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 遇禮拜日，市絕貿易，男女長幼皆沐浴更新衣，以薔薇露或沉香油拭面，焚沉、檀、俺八兒諸香土ＣＬ，人立其上以薰衣，然後往拜。

translations.literal: On prayer days markets cease trade; men and women, old and young, all bathe and put on fresh clothes, wipe their faces with rose dew or agarwood oil, burn fragrant incense powders such as agarwood, sandalwood, and anba'er, stand upon them to fumigate their clothes, and then go to worship.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of prayer commerce halted; everyone bathed, donned clean clothes, and washed their faces with rose water or agarwood oil; fragrant incense powders—agarwood, sandalwood, and anba'er—were burned, and people stood over the smoke to perfume their garments before going to worship.

sentences.zh: 所過街市，香經時不散。

translations.literal: Along the streets passed, fragrance for a long time does not disperse.
translations.idiomatic: The fragrance lingered long in the streets they passed through.

sentences.zh: 天使至，詔書開讀訖，其王遍諭國人，盡出乳香、血竭、蘆薈、沒藥、蘇合油、安息香諸物，與華人交易。

translations.literal: When the imperial envoy arrives and the edict has been opened and read, the king announces it throughout the people; all bring out frankincense, dragon's blood, aloe, myrrh, storax oil, and benzoin and other goods to trade with the Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial envoy arrived and the edict had been read, the king proclaimed it to the whole country; the people brought out frankincense, dragon's blood, aloe, myrrh, storax, and benzoin to trade with the Chinese.

sentences.zh: 乳香乃樹脂。

translations.literal: Frankincense is tree resin.
translations.idiomatic: Frankincense was a tree resin.

sentences.zh: 其樹似榆而葉尖長，土人砍樹取其脂為香。

translations.literal: Its tree resembles the elm but with pointed long leaves; natives cut the tree and take its sap to make incense.
translations.idiomatic: The tree resembled an elm with long pointed leaves; locals cut the bark and collected the sap for incense.

sentences.zh: 有駝雞，頸長類鶴，足高三四尺，毛色若駝，行亦如之，常以充貢。

translations.literal: There is a camel-chicken with a long neck like a crane, legs three or four feet high, fur colored like a camel and walking likewise; it is often sent as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: There was an ostrich with a crane-like neck, legs three or four feet tall, camel-colored plumage, and a camel's gait; it was often sent as tribute.

sentences.zh: 木骨都束

translations.literal: Mugudusuo
translations.idiomatic: Mogadishu

sentences.zh: 木骨都束，自小葛蘭舟行二十晝夜可至。

translations.literal: Mogadishu—from Little Kulam by boat, one can reach it in twenty days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Mogadishu was twenty days' sail by boat from Little Kulam.

sentences.zh: 永樂十四年遣使與不剌哇、麻林諸國奉表朝貢，命鄭和齎敕及幣偕其使者往報之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yongle envoys were sent together with Barawa, Malindi, and other states presenting a memorial and tribute; Zheng He was ordered to carry an edict and silks together with their envoys to respond.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 14 (1416) envoys from Barawa, Malindi, and other states presented tribute; Zheng He was sent with an edict and gifts to accompany their envoys on the return mission.

sentences.zh: 後再入貢，覆命和偕行，賜王及妃彩幣。

translations.literal: Later they entered tribute again; on reporting back He went together with them, bestowing colored silks upon the king and consort.
translations.idiomatic: When they sent tribute again, Zheng He returned with them and granted colored silks to the king and queen.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，貢使又至。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year tribute envoys came again.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute envoys arrived again in the twenty-first year.

sentences.zh: 比還，其王及妃更有賜。

translations.literal: When they returned, the king and consort received further gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On their departure the king and queen received additional gifts.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，和復頒詔其國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande He again issued an edict to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He again proclaimed an imperial edict to the realm.

sentences.zh: 國濱海，山連地曠，磽瘠少收。

translations.literal: The country borders the sea; mountains connect and the land is broad; it is barren and thin with little harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The realm lay on the coast amid linked hills and open country; the soil was poor and yields were scant.

sentences.zh: 歲常旱，或數年不雨。

translations.literal: Years are often drought; sometimes several years pass without rain.
translations.idiomatic: Drought was common, and rain sometimes failed for years on end.

sentences.zh: 俗頑嚚，時操兵習射。

translations.literal: Customs are obstinate and fierce; they often take up arms and practice archery.
translations.idiomatic: The people were rough and warlike, frequently drilling with weapons and practicing archery.

sentences.zh: 地不產木。

translations.literal: The land produces no wood.
translations.idiomatic: Timber did not grow there.

sentences.zh: 亦如忽魯謨斯，壘石為屋，及用魚臘以飼牛羊馬駝雲。

translations.literal: Also like Hormuz, they stack stones for houses, and use dried fish to feed cattle, sheep, horses, and camels, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: As at Hormuz, they built stone houses and fed their cattle, sheep, horses, and camels on dried fish.

sentences.zh: 不剌哇

translations.literal: Bulawa
translations.idiomatic: Barawa

sentences.zh: 不剌哇，與木骨都束接壤。

translations.literal: Barawa—it borders Mogadishu.
translations.idiomatic: Barawa bordered Mogadishu.

sentences.zh: 自錫蘭山別羅里南行，二十一晝夜可至。

translations.literal: From Ceylon's Beruwala, sailing south, one can reach it in twenty-one days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one days' sail south from Beruwala on Ceylon brought one there.

sentences.zh: 永樂十四年至二十一年，凡四入貢，並與木骨都束偕。

translations.literal: From Yongle fourteen to twenty-one, in all four times they entered tribute, always together with Mogadishu.
translations.idiomatic: From Yongle 14 through 21 (1416–1423) they sent tribute four times, always alongside Mogadishu.

sentences.zh: 鄭和亦兩使其國。

translations.literal: Zheng He also twice sent missions to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He visited the realm on two missions.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，和復往使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande He again went on mission.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He returned on mission.

sentences.zh: 其國，傍海而居，地廣斥鹵，少草木，亦壘石為屋。

translations.literal: Its country lives by the sea; the land is broad and saline, with few plants and trees; they also stack stones for houses.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived by the sea on broad saline ground with little vegetation, building their homes of stacked stone.

sentences.zh: 其鹽池。

translations.literal: Its salt pools.
translations.idiomatic: They had salt pans.

sentences.zh: 但投樹枝於中，已而取起，鹽即凝其上。

translations.literal: Simply throw branches into them; after a time they are lifted out, and salt has formed upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Branches were dipped into the brine and later lifted out crusted with salt.

sentences.zh: 俗淳。

translations.literal: Customs are pure.
translations.idiomatic: The people were plain and honest.

sentences.zh: 田不可耕，蒜蔥之外無他種，專捕魚為食。

translations.literal: Fields cannot be cultivated; apart from garlic and scallions there are no other crops; they rely solely on catching fish for food.
translations.idiomatic: The land could not be farmed; apart from garlic and scallions nothing else would grow, and the people lived entirely on fish.

sentences.zh: 所產有馬哈獸，狀如麞；

translations.literal: What they produce includes the maha beast, shaped like a river deer;
translations.idiomatic: Among their products was the maha beast, resembling an antelope;

sentences.zh: 花福祿，狀如驢；

translations.literal: the huafu lu, shaped like a donkey;
translations.idiomatic: the huafu lu, which looked like a donkey;

sentences.zh: 及犀、象、駱駝、沒藥、乳香、龍涎香之類，常以充貢。

translations.literal: and rhinoceros, elephant, camel, myrrh, frankincense, ambergris, and the like—they are often sent as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: along with rhinoceros, elephants, camels, myrrh, frankincense, and ambergris—goods often sent as tribute.

sentences.zh: 竹步，亦與木骨都束接壤。

translations.literal: Zhufu—it also borders Mogadishu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhufu also bordered Mogadishu.

sentences.zh: 永樂中嘗入貢。

translations.literal: During Yongle it once entered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: It sent tribute once during the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 其地戶口不繁，風俗頗淳。

translations.literal: Its land's registered households are not numerous; customs are rather pure.
translations.idiomatic: The population was sparse and the customs comparatively simple.

sentences.zh: 鄭和至其地。

translations.literal: Zheng He reached that land.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He visited the place.

sentences.zh: 地亦無草木，壘石以居，歲多旱暵，皆與木骨都束同。

translations.literal: The land also has no plants or trees; they stack stones to dwell; years often bring drought—all the same as Mogadishu.
translations.idiomatic: The land likewise lacked vegetation; people lived in stone houses, and drought was frequent—conditions much like Mogadishu.

sentences.zh: 所產有獅子、金錢豹、駝蹄雞、龍涎香、乳香、金珀、胡椒之屬。

translations.literal: What they produce includes lions, golden leopards, camel-foot chickens, ambergris, frankincense, golden amber, pepper, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Its products included lions, golden leopards, ostriches, ambergris, frankincense, golden amber, and pepper.

sentences.zh: 阿丹，在古裡之西，順風二十二晝夜可至。

translations.literal: Aden—it lies west of Calicut; with a fair wind one can reach it in twenty-two days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Aden lay west of Calicut, twenty-two days' sail with a fair wind.

sentences.zh: 永樂十四年遣使奉表貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yongle envoys were sent presenting a memorial and local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 14 (1416) envoys arrived with a memorial and local tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 辭還，命鄭和齎敕及彩幣偕往賜之。

translations.literal: On taking leave to return, Zheng He was ordered to carry an edict and colored silks to go together and bestow them.
translations.idiomatic: When they prepared to depart, Zheng He was sent with an edict and colored silks to accompany them home with imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 自是，凡四入貢，天子亦厚加賜賚。

translations.literal: From then on, in all four times they entered tribute; the Son of Heaven also lavishly added gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute four times, and the emperor richly rewarded each mission.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，海外諸番久缺貢，覆命和齎敕宣諭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande the various overseas fan states had long lacked tribute; again He was ordered to carry an edict to proclaim and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430), after long silence from the maritime states, Zheng He was again dispatched with an edict of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 其王抹立克那思兒即遣使來貢。

translations.literal: Its king Mubarak Nasir immediately dispatched envoys to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: King Mubarak Nasir promptly sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年至京師。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They reached the capital in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 正統元年始還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong they only then returned.
translations.idiomatic: They did not return home until Zhengtong 1 (1436).

sentences.zh: 自後，天朝不復通使，遠番貢使亦不至。

translations.literal: After that the Celestial Court no longer sent envoys, and distant fan tribute envoys also did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the court sent no further missions, and tribute envoys from the distant maritime states ceased to come.

sentences.zh: 前世梁、隋、唐時，並有丹丹國，或言即其地。

translations.literal: In earlier ages during Liang, Sui, and Tang there was also the Dandan country; some say it is that place.
translations.idiomatic: The Dandan realm of Liang, Sui, and Tang times was identified by some with this same land.

sentences.zh: 地膏腴，饒粟麥。

translations.literal: The land is fertile and rich in millet and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was rich and millet and wheat were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 人性強悍，有馬步銳卒七八千人，鄰邦畏之。

translations.literal: People's nature is fierce and strong; they have seven or eight thousand elite infantry and cavalry; neighboring states fear them.
translations.idiomatic: The people were warlike, fielding seven or eight thousand crack troops, and their neighbors feared them.

sentences.zh: 王及國人悉奉回回教。

translations.literal: The king and the people of the country all follow the Hui Muslim religion.
translations.idiomatic: The king and his subjects were Muslims.

sentences.zh: 氣候常和，歲不置閏。

translations.literal: The climate is always mild; years do not insert intercalary months.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was mild year-round, and their calendar had no intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 其定時之法，以月為準，如今夜見新月，明日即為月朔。

translations.literal: Their method of fixing time takes the month as standard—as if tonight one sees the new moon, tomorrow is the month's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: They reckoned time by the lunar month: sight the new moon tonight, and tomorrow is the first of the month.

sentences.zh: 四季不定，自有陰陽家推算。

translations.literal: The four seasons are not fixed; yin-yang specialists calculate them.
translations.idiomatic: The seasons had no fixed calendar dates; specialists in yin-yang lore calculated them.

sentences.zh: 其日為春首，即有花開；

translations.literal: The day that is the head of spring, flowers immediately bloom;
translations.idiomatic: On the day marked as spring's beginning, flowers opened;

sentences.zh: 其日為秋初，即有葉落；

translations.literal: the day that is autumn's beginning, leaves immediately fall;
translations.idiomatic: on the day marked as autumn's beginning, leaves fell;

sentences.zh: 及日月交食、風雨潮汐，皆能預測。

translations.literal: and solar and lunar eclipses, wind and rain, and tides—they can all be predicted.
translations.idiomatic: and they could forecast eclipses, weather, and the tides.

sentences.zh: 其王甚尊中國。

translations.literal: Its king greatly respects China.
translations.idiomatic: The king held China in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 聞和船至，躬率部領來迎。

translations.literal: Hearing He's fleet has arrived, he personally leads his retinue to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Zheng He's fleet had arrived, he personally led his officials out to welcome it.

sentences.zh: 入國宣詔訖，遍諭其下，盡出珍寶互易。

translations.literal: Entering the country, after the edict is proclaimed, he announces it throughout his subordinates; all bring out precious treasures for mutual exchange.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict was proclaimed in the capital, he made it known throughout the realm, and the people brought out precious goods to trade.

sentences.zh: 永樂十九年，中官周姓者往，市得貓睛，重二錢許，珊瑚樹高二尺者數枝，又大珠、金珀、諸色雅姑異寶、麒麟、獅子、花貓、鹿、金錢豹、駝雞、白鳩以歸，他國所不及也。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yongle a eunuch surnamed Zhou went; at market he obtained cat's-eye stones weighing about two qian, several coral trees two chi high, and also large pearls, golden amber, various colored yakut precious things, qilin, lions, flower cats, deer, golden leopards, camel-chickens, and white doves to return—other countries could not match it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 19 (1421) a eunuch surnamed Zhou went there and bought cat's-eyes weighing about two mace, several two-foot coral trees, large pearls, golden amber, gems of many hues, giraffes, lions, leopards, deer, golden leopards, ostriches, and white doves—treasures no other realm could equal.

sentences.zh: 蔬果、畜產咸備，獨無鵝、豕二者。

translations.literal: Fruits, vegetables, and livestock are all complete; only geese and pigs are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Fruit, vegetables, and livestock were plentiful, but geese and pigs were absent.

sentences.zh: 市肆有書籍。

translations.literal: Market stalls have books.
translations.idiomatic: Books were sold in the markets.

sentences.zh: 工人所制金首飾，絕勝諸蕃。

translations.literal: Gold head ornaments that craftsmen make surpass all the fan states.
translations.idiomatic: Gold jewelry made by local craftsmen surpassed anything found among the maritime states.

sentences.zh: 所少惟無草木，其居亦皆壘石為之。

translations.literal: What is lacking is only the absence of plants and trees; their dwellings also are all made by stacking stone.
translations.idiomatic: The only scarcity was vegetation; even the houses were built of stacked stone.

sentences.zh: 麒麟前足高九尺，後六尺，頸長丈六尺有二，短角，牛尾，鹿身，食粟豆餅餌。
