translations.literal: The qilin's front legs are nine chi high, rear six chi; the neck is one zhang, six chi, and two cun long; short horns, ox tail, deer body; it eats millet, beans, cakes, and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: The giraffe stood nine feet at the forelegs and six at the hind, with a neck sixteen feet two inches long, short horns, an ox's tail, and a deer's body; it fed on millet, beans, and cakes.

sentences.zh: 獅子形似虎，黑黃色無斑，首大、口廣、尾尖，聲吼若雷，百獸見之皆伏地。

translations.literal: The lion's form resembles a tiger, black-yellow in color without stripes; head large, mouth broad, tail pointed; its roar is like thunder; the hundred beasts seeing it all prostrate on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The lion resembled a tiger, tawny and unmarked; its head was large, its maw wide, and its tail tapered; its roar thundered, and every beast fell prostrate at the sight.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時制方丘朝日壇玉爵，購紅黃玉於天方、哈密諸蕃，不可得。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period, when making the jade libation cup for the Square Mound and Sun Altar, red and yellow jade was sought from Tianfang, Hami, and other fan states, but could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign, when crafting the jade libation cup for the Square Mound and Sun Altar, the court sought red and yellow jade from Tianfang, Hami, and other western regions without success.

sentences.zh: 有通事言此玉產於阿丹，去土魯番西南二千里，其地兩山對峙，自為雌雄，或自鳴，請如永樂、宣德故事，齎重賄往購。

translations.literal: An interpreter said this jade is produced at Aden, two thousand li southwest of Turfan; at that place two mountains face each other as male and female, sometimes sounding of themselves; he requested that, following the precedent of Yongle and Xuande, heavy bribes be carried to go purchase it.
translations.idiomatic: An interpreter reported that the jade came from Aden, two thousand li southwest of Turfan, where two facing mountains were said to be male and female and sometimes to resound on their own; he asked that, as in the Yongle and Xuande reigns, a richly laden mission be sent to buy it.

sentences.zh: 帝從部議，已之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed the ministry's deliberation and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the ministry's advice and dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 剌撒，自古裡順風二十晝夜可至。

translations.literal: Las'a—from Calicut, with a fair wind one can reach it in twenty days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Las'a was twenty days' sail with a fair wind from Calicut.

sentences.zh: 永樂十四年遣使來貢，命鄭和報之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yongle envoys were sent to present tribute; Zheng He was ordered to respond.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 14 (1416) tribute envoys arrived, and Zheng He was dispatched to return the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 後凡三貢，皆與阿丹、不剌哇諸國偕。

translations.literal: Later, in all three times they presented tribute, always together with Aden, Barawa, and other states.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute three more times, always together with Aden, Barawa, and the other states.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，和復齎敕往使，竟不復貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande He again carried an edict on mission; in the end they never again presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He returned with an edict, but no further tribute ever came.

sentences.zh: 國傍海而居，氣候常熱，田瘠少收。

translations.literal: The country lives by the sea; the climate is always hot; fields are thin with little harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived by the sea in a perpetually hot climate, and the poor soil yielded little.

sentences.zh: 俗淳，喪葬有禮。

translations.literal: Customs are pure; funeral and burial have ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The customs were simple and honest, and funerals were conducted with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 有事則禱鬼神。

translations.literal: When there is a matter, then they pray to ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble arose, they prayed to spirits and deities.

sentences.zh: 草木不生，久旱不雨。

translations.literal: Plants and trees do not grow; long drought brings no rain.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing green would grow, and prolonged drought brought no rain.

sentences.zh: 居室，悉與竹步諸國同。

translations.literal: Dwellings—all are the same as the countries of Zhufu and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Their houses were much like those of Zhufu and the neighboring realms.

sentences.zh: 所產有乳香、龍涎香、千里駝之類。

translations.literal: What it produces includes frankincense, ambergris, thousand-li camels, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Local products included frankincense, ambergris, dromedaries, and the like.

sentences.zh: 麻林，去中國絕遠。

translations.literal: Malindi—it is extremely far from China.
translations.idiomatic: Malindi lay at the farthest remove from China.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年遣使貢麒麟。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle envoys were sent to present tribute of a qilin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 13 (1415) it sent envoys bearing a giraffe as tribute.

sentences.zh: 將至，禮部尚書呂震請表賀，帝曰：「往儒臣進《五經四書大全》，請上表，朕許之，以此書有益於治也。

translations.literal: When it was about to arrive, Minister of Rites Lü Zhen requested a celebratory memorial; the emperor said: "Previously when Confucian officials presented the Great Compendium of the Five Classics and Four Books, they asked to submit a memorial and I permitted it, because that book benefits governance.
translations.idiomatic: As the tribute mission neared, Minister of Rites Lü Zhen asked to submit a congratulatory memorial. The emperor said, "When scholars once presented the Great Compendium of the Five Classics and Four Books and asked to memorialize the court, I allowed it because that work truly served good government.

sentences.zh: 麟之有無，何所損益，其已之。」

translations.literal: Whether there is a qilin or not—what loss or gain is there? Let it be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Whether a qilin appears or not makes no difference one way or the other. Drop the matter.

sentences.zh: 已而麻林與諸蕃使者以麟及天馬、神鹿諸物進，帝御奉天門受之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Malindi together with envoys from the various fan realms presented a qilin along with heavenly horses, divine deer, and other things; the emperor attended at Fengtian Gate to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward, Malindi and the other foreign envoys presented a giraffe together with heavenly horses, sacred deer, and other exotic gifts, and the emperor received them in state at Fengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 百僚稽首稱賀，帝曰：「此皇考厚德所致，亦賴卿等翊贊，故遠人畢來。

translations.literal: The hundred officials kowtowed and offered congratulations; the emperor said: "This is brought about by my late father's deep virtue, and also relies on your support and assistance, hence distant people all come.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials kowtowed in congratulation. The emperor said, "This comes from my late father's accumulated virtue, and from your loyal support as well—that is why peoples from afar gather here.

sentences.zh: 繼自今，益宜秉德迪朕不逮。」

translations.literal: From now on, you should all the more uphold virtue and guide where I fall short."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth you must hold still more firmly to virtue and help me where I fall short.

sentences.zh: 十四年又貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year they again presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year they sent tribute goods again.

sentences.zh: 忽魯謨斯

translations.literal: Hulumosi
translations.idiomatic: Hormuz

sentences.zh: 忽魯謨斯，西洋大國也。

translations.literal: Hormuz—it is a great country of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Hormuz was a major power of the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 自古裡西北行，二十五日可至。

translations.literal: From Calicut, going northwest, one can reach it in twenty-five days.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five days' sail northwest from Calicut brought one there.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年，天子以西洋近國已航海貢琛，稽顙闕下，而遠者猶未賓服，乃命鄭和齎璽書往諸國，賜其王錦綺、彩帛、紗羅，妃及大臣皆有賜。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle, the Son of Heaven, because the near countries of the Western Ocean had already come by sea to present tribute gems and kowtowed at the palace gate, while distant ones had still not submitted, then ordered Zheng He to carry the imperial seal letter to the various countries, bestowing upon their kings brocades, colored silks, and gauzes; the consorts and great ministers all received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 10 (1412), noting that the nearer maritime states had already sailed to court with tribute and prostrated themselves before the throne while remoter realms had not yet submitted, the emperor ordered Zheng He to carry imperial letters to those countries and grant their kings brocades, colored silks, and gauzes; queens and ministers received gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 王即遣陪臣已即丁奉金葉表，貢馬及方物。

translations.literal: The king immediately sent attendant minister Yijiding bearing a gold-leaf memorial, presenting horses and local products.
translations.idiomatic: The king at once dispatched his minister Yijiding with a memorial on gold leaf, offering horses and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年至京師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They reached the capital in the twelfth year.

sentences.zh: 命禮官宴賜，酬以馬直。

translations.literal: Ritual officials were ordered to feast and bestow gifts, compensating them with the price of the horses.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered ritual officials to feast and reward them, paying the full value of the horses.

sentences.zh: 比還，賜王及妃以下有差。

translations.literal: When they returned, the king, consort, and those below received differentiated gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On their departure, the king, queen, and their party received gifts in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 自是凡四貢。

translations.literal: From this time there were in all four tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they sent tribute four times in all.

sentences.zh: 和亦再使。

translations.literal: He also went on mission twice.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He visited twice as well.

sentences.zh: 後朝使不往，其使亦不來。

translations.literal: Later court envoys did not go, and their envoys also did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward imperial missions ceased, and Hormuz sent no envoys either.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年復遣和宣詔其國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande He was again dispatched to proclaim an edict to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He was again sent to proclaim an imperial edict to the realm.

sentences.zh: 其王賽弗丁乃遣使來貢。

translations.literal: Its king Saifuding then sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: King Saifuddin thereupon sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年至京師，宴賜有加。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they reached the capital; feasting and gifts were increased.
translations.idiomatic: They reached the capital in the eighth year and received an especially generous feast and gifts.

sentences.zh: 正統元年附爪哇舟還國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong they returned home aboard a Javanese vessel.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 (1436) they sailed home on a Javanese ship.

sentences.zh: 嗣後遂絕。

translations.literal: After this contact ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After that the tribute missions ended.

sentences.zh: 其國居西海之極。

translations.literal: Its country dwells at the extreme of the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The realm stood at the western edge of the ocean.

sentences.zh: 自東南諸蠻邦及大西洋商舶、西域賈人，皆來貿易，故寶物填溢。

translations.literal: From the various man states of the southeast, Atlantic merchant ships, and Western Regions traders, all came to trade; hence precious things overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants from the southeastern barbarian states, Atlantic trade fleets, and Western traders all gathered to exchange goods, and precious commodities filled the markets.

sentences.zh: 氣候有寒暑，春發葩，秋隕葉，有霜無雪，多露少雨。

translations.literal: The climate has cold and heat; in spring blossoms open, in autumn leaves fall; there is frost but no snow, much dew and little rain.
translations.idiomatic: The climate knew both cold and heat: flowers opened in spring and leaves fell in autumn; frost came but not snow, and dew was plentiful while rain was scarce.

sentences.zh: 土瘠穀麥寡，然他方轉輸者多，故價殊賤。

translations.literal: The soil is thin and grain and wheat are few; yet because much is transported in from other places, prices are exceptionally cheap.
translations.idiomatic: The land was poor and grain scarce, but because so much was shipped in from abroad, prices were remarkably low.

sentences.zh: 民富俗厚，或遭禍致貧，眾皆遺以錢帛，共振助之。

translations.literal: The people are wealthy and customs generous; if someone meets disaster and becomes poor, the multitude all leave them money and cloth, together rallying to help.
translations.idiomatic: The people were prosperous and customs humane: when misfortune reduced someone to poverty, neighbors gave money and cloth and joined together in mutual aid.

sentences.zh: 人多白晰豐偉，婦女出則以紗蔽面，市列廛肆，百物具備。

translations.literal: People are mostly fair-skinned, tall, and robust; when women go out they cover their faces with gauze; the market lines shops and stalls, and the hundred things are all complete.
translations.idiomatic: Most people were fair-complexioned and sturdily built; women veiled their faces in gauze when they went abroad; market streets were lined with shops stocked with every sort of goods.

sentences.zh: 惟禁酒，犯者罪至死。

translations.literal: Only wine is forbidden; offenders are punished up to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wine alone was forbidden, and violators could be punished with death.

sentences.zh: 醫卜、技藝，皆類中華。

translations.literal: Medicine, divination, and crafts all resemble China.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine, divination, and the arts all resembled those of China.

sentences.zh: 交易用銀錢。

translations.literal: In trade they use silver coins.
translations.idiomatic: Trade was conducted in silver coin.

sentences.zh: 書用回回字。

translations.literal: Writing uses Huihui script.
translations.idiomatic: Writing employed Arabic script.

sentences.zh: 王及臣下皆遵回教，婚喪悉用其禮。

translations.literal: The king and officials below all follow the Hui religion; weddings and funerals all use its rites.
translations.idiomatic: The king and his subjects all followed Islam, and weddings and funerals were conducted by its rites.

sentences.zh: 日齋戒沐浴，虔拜者五。

translations.literal: Daily they fast, bathe in purification, and devoutly worship five times.
translations.idiomatic: Each day they purified themselves through ablution and performed five devout prayers.

sentences.zh: 地多咸，不產草木，牛羊馬駝皆啖魚臘。

translations.literal: The land is much salty; it does not produce plants and trees; cattle, sheep, horses, and camels all eat dried fish.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the soil was saline and bore no vegetation; cattle, sheep, horses, and camels were all fed on dried fish.

sentences.zh: 壘石為屋，有三四層者，寢處庖廁及待客之所，咸在其上。

translations.literal: They pile stones to make houses; some have three or four stories; sleeping quarters, kitchens, latrines, and places for receiving guests are all above.
translations.idiomatic: They built stone houses, some three or four stories high, with bedrooms, kitchens, privies, and guest rooms all on the upper floors.

sentences.zh: 饒蔬果，有核桃、把聃、松子、石榴、葡萄、花紅、萬年棗之屬。

translations.literal: Fruits and vegetables are abundant; there are walnuts, badam, pine nuts, pomegranates, grapes, huahong, and ten-thousand-year jujubes, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Fruit and vegetables were plentiful, including walnuts, almonds, pine nuts, pomegranates, grapes, pears, jujubes, and the like.

sentences.zh: 境內有大山，四面異色。

translations.literal: Within the borders are great mountains; on four sides the colors differ.
translations.idiomatic: Great mountains within the realm showed a different color on each face.

sentences.zh: 一紅鹽石，鑿以為器，盛食物不加鹽，而味自和；

translations.literal: One is red salt stone; carved to make vessels, when holding food without adding salt, the flavor naturally harmonizes;
translations.idiomatic: One slope yielded red salt rock that could be carved into vessels: food placed in them needed no added salt, yet tasted perfectly seasoned;

sentences.zh: 一白土，可涂垣壁；

translations.literal: one is white earth, usable to plaster walls;
translations.idiomatic: another gave white clay fit for whitewashing walls;

sentences.zh: 一赤土、一黃土，皆適於用。

translations.literal: one red earth and one yellow earth—all suitable for use.
translations.idiomatic: and red and yellow earths, each useful in its own way.

sentences.zh: 所貢有獅子、麒麟、駝雞、福祿、靈羊；

translations.literal: What they presented in tribute includes lions, qilin, camel-chickens, fulu, and spirit sheep;
translations.idiomatic: Tribute animals included lions, giraffes, ostriches, zebras, and antelope;

sentences.zh: 常貢則大珠、寶石之類。

translations.literal: Regular tribute then includes large pearls, precious stones, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: ordinary tribute consisted of large pearls, gems, and the like.

sentences.zh: 溜山 比剌

translations.literal: Liushan Bila
translations.idiomatic: Liushan and Bira

sentences.zh: 溜山，自錫蘭山別羅里南去，順風七晝夜可至；

translations.literal: Liushan—from Ceylon's Beruwala going south, with a fair wind one can reach it in seven days and nights;
translations.idiomatic: Liushan lay seven days' sail with a fair wind south from Beruwala in Ceylon;

sentences.zh: 自蘇門答剌過小帽山西南行，十晝夜可至。

translations.literal: from Samudra passing Little Hat Mountain going southwest, one can reach it in ten days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: or ten days' sail southwest from Samudra past Little Hat Mountain.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年，鄭和往使其國。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle Zheng He went on mission to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 10 (1412) Zheng He was dispatched on mission there.

sentences.zh: 十四年，其王亦速福遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year its king Yisufu sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year King Yusuf sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 自後三貢，並與忽魯謨斯諸國偕。

translations.literal: After this there were three tribute missions, all together with Hormuz and the other countries.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute three more times, always together with Hormuz and the other states.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，鄭和復使其國，後竟不至。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande Zheng He again went on mission to their country; afterward they never came.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He visited again, but no further missions ever came.

sentences.zh: 其山居海中，有三石門，並可通舟。

translations.literal: Its mountains stand in the sea; there are three stone gates, all passable by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Its islands rose from the sea, with three stone channels through which boats could pass.

sentences.zh: 無城郭，倚山聚居。

translations.literal: There are no walls and moats; they lean on the mountains to gather and dwell.
translations.idiomatic: There were no walled cities; the people clustered along the hillsides.

sentences.zh: 氣候常熱，土薄谷少，無麥，土人皆捕魚，暴乾以充食。

translations.literal: The climate is always hot; soil is thin and grain few; there is no wheat; the native people all catch fish and dry them in the sun to serve as food.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was perpetually hot, the soil poor and grain scarce, and wheat absent; the people lived mainly on fish caught and sun-dried for food.

sentences.zh: 王及群下盡回回人，婚喪諸禮，多類忽魯謨斯。

translations.literal: The king and the multitude below are all Hui people; wedding, funeral, and other rites mostly resemble Hormuz.
translations.idiomatic: The king and his people were all Muslims, and their wedding and funeral customs largely matched those of Hormuz.

sentences.zh: 山下有八溜，或言外更有三千溜，舟或失風入其處，即沉溺。

translations.literal: Below the mountains are eight liu; some say beyond there are three thousand more liu; if a boat loses the wind and enters such a place, it immediately sinks.
translations.idiomatic: Eight channels lay below the hills, and some said three thousand more beyond; any vessel driven off course into them was lost.

sentences.zh: 又有國曰比剌，曰孫剌。

translations.literal: There are also countries called Bila and called Sunla.
translations.idiomatic: Two other states were called Bila and Sunla.

sentences.zh: 鄭和亦嘗齎敕往賜。

translations.literal: Zheng He also once carried an edict to go and bestow gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He also once carried an imperial edict and gifts to them.

sentences.zh: 以去中華絕遠，二國貢使竟不至。

translations.literal: Because they were extremely far from China, the two countries' tribute envoys in the end never came.
translations.idiomatic: They were so far from China that neither realm ever sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 南巫裡

translations.literal: Nan Wuli
translations.idiomatic: Nanwuli

sentences.zh: 南巫裡，在西南海中。

translations.literal: Nanwuli—it is in the southwestern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Nanwuli lay in the southwestern seas.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年遣使齎璽書、彩幣撫諭其國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle envoys were sent carrying the imperial seal letter and colored silks to soothe and instruct their country.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 (1405) envoys were sent with an imperial letter and colored silks to offer reassurance to the realm.

sentences.zh: 六年，鄭和復往使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zheng He again went on mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zheng He visited again.

sentences.zh: 九年，其王遣使貢方物，與急蘭丹、加異勒諸國偕來。

translations.literal: In the ninth year its king sent envoys presenting local products, coming together with Kelantan, Kayal, and the other countries.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year its king sent envoys with local tribute, arriving together with Kelantan, Kayal, and other states.

sentences.zh: 賜其王金織文綺、金繡龍衣、銷金幃幔及傘蓋諸物，命禮官宴賜遣之。

translations.literal: They were granted gold-woven patterned brocades, gold-embroidered dragon robes, gold-trimmed curtains and canopies, and other things; ritual officials were ordered to feast, bestow gifts, and send them off.
translations.idiomatic: The king received gold-woven brocades, dragon robes embroidered in gold, gilded curtains and parasols, and other gifts; ritual officials feasted the envoys, rewarded them, and saw them on their way.

sentences.zh: 十四年再貢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year they again presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 命鄭和與其使偕行，後不復至。

translations.literal: Zheng He was ordered to travel together with their envoys; afterward they never came again.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He was ordered to return with their envoys, but no further missions followed.

sentences.zh: 加異勒

translations.literal: Jiayile
translations.idiomatic: Kayal

sentences.zh: 加異勒，西洋小國也。

translations.literal: Kayal—it is a small country of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Kayal was a small state of the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年遣鄭和齎詔招諭，賜以錦綺、紗羅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle Zheng He was sent carrying an edict to summon and instruct them, bestowing brocades and gauzes.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 6 (1408) Zheng He was dispatched with an edict of invitation and granted brocades and gauzes.

sentences.zh: 九年，其酋長葛卜者麻遣使奉表，貢方物。

translations.literal: In the ninth year its chieftain Gebozhema sent envoys presenting a memorial and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year its chief Gebozhe Ma sent envoys with a memorial and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 命賜宴及冠帶、彩幣、寶鈔。

translations.literal: They were ordered to be granted a feast, cap and belt, colored silks, and treasure notes.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a feast and gifts of official cap and belt, colored silks, and paper money.

sentences.zh: 十年，和再使其國，後凡三入貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year He again went on mission to their country; afterward in all they entered tribute three times.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zheng He visited again, and they sent tribute three more times thereafter.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，和復使其國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande He again went on mission to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He visited the realm again.

sentences.zh: 八年又偕阿丹等十一國來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they again came to present tribute together with Aden and eleven other countries.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year they came again with Aden and ten other states to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 甘巴裡

translations.literal: Ganbali
translations.idiomatic: Cambay

sentences.zh: 甘巴裡，亦西洋小國。

translations.literal: Cambay—it is also a small country of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Cambay was likewise a small state of the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年，鄭和使其地，賜其王錦綺、紗羅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle Zheng He went on mission to that place, bestowing upon its king brocades and gauzes.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 6 (1408) Zheng He visited and granted the king brocades and gauzes.

sentences.zh: 十三年遣使朝貢方物。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year envoys were sent to court to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year it sent envoys to court with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 十九年再貢，遣鄭和報之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year they again presented tribute; Zheng He was dispatched to respond.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again in the nineteenth year, and Zheng He was dispatched to return the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，和復招諭其國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande He again summoned and instructed their country.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 (1430) Zheng He again carried an edict of reassurance to the realm.

sentences.zh: 王兜哇剌札遣使來貢，八年抵京師。

translations.literal: King Douwala Zha sent envoys to present tribute; in the eighth year they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: King Douwala Zha sent envoys with tribute, and they reached the capital in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 正統元年附爪哇舟還國，賜敕勞王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong they returned home aboard a Javanese vessel; an edict was bestowed to console the king.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 (1436) they sailed home on a Javanese ship, and the emperor granted an edict commending the king.

sentences.zh: 其鄰境有阿撥把丹、小阿蘭二國，亦以六年命鄭和齎敕招諭，賜亦同。

translations.literal: On its borders are the two countries Abobadan and Little Oman; likewise in the sixth year Zheng He was ordered to carry an edict to summon and instruct them; the gifts were also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Two neighboring states, Abobadan and Little Oman, were likewise visited in the sixth year when Zheng He carried edicts of invitation; the gifts granted were the same.

sentences.zh: 急蘭丹

translations.literal: Jilandan
translations.idiomatic: Kelantan

sentences.zh: 急蘭丹，永樂九年，王麻哈剌查苦馬兒遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Kelantan—in the ninth year of Yongle King Mahala Cha Kuma'er sent envoys to court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Kelantan: in Yongle 9 (1411) King Mahala Cha Kuma'er sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十年命鄭和齎敕獎其王，賚以錦綺、紗羅、彩帛。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zheng He was ordered to carry an edict rewarding its king, bestowing brocades, gauzes, and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zheng He was sent with an edict commending the king and bearing brocades, gauzes, and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 沙裡灣泥

translations.literal: Shaliwanni
translations.idiomatic: Sarwani

sentences.zh: 沙裡灣泥，永樂十四年遣使來獻方物，命鄭和齎幣帛還賜之。

translations.literal: Sarwani—in the fourteenth year of Yongle envoys were sent to present local products; Zheng He was ordered to carry silks and cloth to return and bestow gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Sarwani: in Yongle 14 (1416) it sent envoys with local tribute, and Zheng He was ordered to carry silks back with gifts in return.

sentences.zh: 底里，永樂十年遣使奉璽書招諭其王馬哈木，賜絨錦、金織文綺、彩帛諸物。

translations.literal: Delhi—in the tenth year of Yongle envoys were sent bearing the imperial seal letter to summon and instruct its king Mahmud, bestowing velvet brocades, gold-woven patterned brocades, colored silks, and other things.
translations.idiomatic: Delhi: in Yongle 10 (1412) envoys were sent with an imperial letter to summon King Mahmud, granting velvet brocades, gold-woven brocades, colored silks, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 其地與沼納朴兒近，並賜其王亦不剌金。

translations.literal: Its land is near Gawadar; its king Ibrahim was also bestowed gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm lay near Gawadar, its king Ibrahim received gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 千里達

translations.literal: Qianlida
translations.idiomatic: Qalhat

sentences.zh: 千里達，永樂十六年遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: Qalhat—in the sixteenth year of Yongle envoys were sent to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: Qalhat: in Yongle 16 (1418) it sent envoys with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 賜其使冠帶、纟寧絲、紗羅、彩帛及寶鈔。

translations.literal: Its envoys were granted cap and belt, fine silk, gauze, colored silks, and treasure notes.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were granted official cap and belt, fine silk, gauze, colored silks, and paper money.

sentences.zh: 比還，賜其王有加。

translations.literal: When they returned, the king received increased gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On their departure the king received additional gifts.

sentences.zh: 失剌比

translations.literal: Shilabi
translations.idiomatic: Shiraz

sentences.zh: 失剌比，永樂十六年遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Shilabi—in the sixteenth year of Yongle sent envoys to court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Shiraz: in Yongle 16 (1418) it sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 賜其使冠帶、金織文綺、襲衣、彩幣、白金有差，其王亦優賜。

translations.literal: Its envoys were granted cap and belt, gold-woven patterned brocades, ceremonial robes, colored silks, and white silver in varying amounts; its king also received generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys received official cap and belt, gold-woven brocades, ceremonial robes, colored silks, and silver in graded amounts, and the king was likewise favored with generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 古裡班卒

translations.literal: Guli Banzu
translations.idiomatic: Gur Bandar

sentences.zh: 古裡班卒，永樂中，嘗入貢。

translations.literal: Gur Bandar—during the Yongle reign, once presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Gur Bandar: during the Yongle era it once sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 其土瘠谷少，物產亦薄。

translations.literal: Its soil is barren and grain scarce; local products are also meager.
translations.idiomatic: The land was poor and grain scarce, and its products were likewise thin.

sentences.zh: 氣候不齊，夏多雨，雨即寒。

translations.literal: The climate is uneven; in summer there is much rain, and when it rains it turns cold.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was changeable: summers brought heavy rain, and rain brought sudden cold.

sentences.zh: 白葛達 黑葛達

translations.literal: Bai Geda; Hei Geda
translations.idiomatic: White Gur Dad and Black Gur Dad

sentences.zh: 白葛達，宣德元年遣其臣和者裡一思入貢。

translations.literal: White Gur Dad—in the first year of Xuande sent its minister Hezheli Yisi to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: White Gur Dad: in Xuande 1 (1426) it sent the minister Hezheli Yisi with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其使臣言：「遭風破舟，貢物盡失，國主惓惓忠敬之忱，無由上達。

translations.literal: Its envoy said: "We met wind and our vessel was wrecked; the tribute goods were all lost. The king's earnest loyal devotion could not reach above.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported: "A storm wrecked our ship and all the tribute was lost, so our king's earnest loyalty could not reach Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 此使臣之罪，惟聖天子恩貸，賜之冠帶，俾得歸見國主，知陪臣實詣闕廷，庶幾免責。」

translations.literal: This is the envoy's crime; only if the sage Son of Heaven graciously pardons and bestows cap and belt, allowing return to see the king and know that the attendant minister truly reached the imperial court, might blame be escaped."
translations.idiomatic: The fault is mine alone. I beg the Son of Heaven to show mercy, grant me cap and belt, and let me return to my king so he may know his minister truly reached the court—then perhaps I may be spared punishment."

sentences.zh: 帝許之，使附鄰國貢舟還國，諭之曰：「倉卒失風，豈人力能制。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, had him attach to a neighboring state's tribute vessel to return home, and instructed him: "A sudden storm at sea—how could human power control it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented and sent him home on a neighboring tribute ship, telling him: "A sudden storm at sea is no fault of yours.

sentences.zh: 歸語爾主，朕嘉王之誠，不在物也。」

translations.literal: Return and tell your lord: I commend the king's sincerity; it lies not in the goods."
translations.idiomatic: Tell your king when you return that I honor his sincerity, not the tribute itself."

sentences.zh: 宴賜悉如禮。

translations.literal: Banquets and gifts were all according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He was entertained and rewarded fully according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 及辭歸，帝謂禮官曰：「天時漸寒，海道遼遠，可賜路費及衣服。」

translations.literal: When he took leave to return, the emperor told the ritual officials: "The season is turning cold and the sea route is long and far; traveling expenses and clothing may be granted."
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to depart, the emperor told the Ministry of Rites: "The weather is turning cold and the voyage home is long—give him traveling funds and clothes."

sentences.zh: 其國，土地瘠薄，崇釋教，市易用鐵錢。

translations.literal: That country has thin, poor land, venerates the Buddhist teaching, and uses iron coins in market exchange.
translations.idiomatic: The realm itself had poor soil, honored Buddhism, and used iron coins in trade.

sentences.zh: 又有黑葛達，亦以宣德時來貢。

translations.literal: There is also Black Gur Dad, which likewise came to present tribute in the Xuande reign.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Black Gur Dad, which likewise sent tribute during the Xuande era.

sentences.zh: 國小民貧，尚佛畏刑。

translations.literal: The state is small and the people poor; they esteem the Buddha and fear punishment.
translations.idiomatic: It was a small, impoverished realm whose people revered Buddhism and feared the law.

sentences.zh: 多牛羊，亦以鐵鑄錢。

translations.literal: Cattle and sheep are plentiful; iron is also cast into coins.
translations.idiomatic: Cattle and sheep were abundant, and iron was cast into coin as well.

sentences.zh: 拂菻

translations.literal: Fulin
translations.idiomatic: Byzantium

sentences.zh: 〈（即東羅馬帝國，又稱“拜占庭帝國”）〉，

translations.literal: (namely the Eastern Roman Empire, also called the "Byzantine Empire")〉,
translations.idiomatic: that is, the Eastern Roman Empire, also known as the Byzantine Empire)〉,

sentences.zh: 即漢大秦，桓帝時始通中國。

translations.literal: which is the Han-era Da Qin; contact with China began in Emperor Huan's reign.
translations.idiomatic: the Da Qin known to the Han—first contact with China came in the reign of Emperor Huan.

sentences.zh: 晉及魏皆曰大秦，嘗入貢。

translations.literal: Under Jin and Wei it was all called Da Qin, and once presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin and Wei dynasties likewise called it Da Qin, and it sent tribute on occasion.

sentences.zh: 唐曰拂菻，宋仍之，亦數入貢。

translations.literal: Tang called it Fulin; Song kept the name, and it also repeatedly presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang renamed it Fulin; the Song kept the term, and tribute missions came several times.

sentences.zh: 而《宋史》謂歷代未嘗朝貢，疑其非大秦也。

translations.literal: Yet the Song History says that through successive dynasties it never came to court with tribute, raising doubt that it was Da Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Song History, however, says it never sent tribute through the ages, which casts doubt on its identification with Da Qin.

sentences.zh: 元末，其國人捏古倫入市中國，元亡不能歸。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan, a man of that country named Niegu Lun entered the market in China; when Yuan fell he could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuan, a subject of Fulin named Niegu Lun came to trade in China and was stranded when the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，以洪武四年八月召見，命齎詔書還諭其王曰：「自有宋失馭，天絕其祀。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor heard of it; in the eighth month of the fourth year of Hongwu he summoned and received him, ordered him to carry an edict back and instruct its king, saying: "Since Song lost control, Heaven cut off its sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongwu Emperor learned of this, he summoned Niegu Lun in the eighth month of Hongwu 4 (1371) and sent him home with an edict for the king: "Since the Song lost the Mandate, Heaven ended their line.

sentences.zh: 元興沙漠，入主中國百有餘年，天厭其昏淫，亦用隕絕其命。

translations.literal: Yuan rose from the desert and ruled China for more than a hundred years; Heaven grew weary of its debauchery and likewise ended its mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan rose from the desert and ruled China for more than a century, until Heaven, sickened by their corruption, cut short their reign as well.

sentences.zh: 中原擾亂十有八年，當群雄初起時，朕為淮右布衣，起義救民。

translations.literal: The Central Plain was disturbed for eighteen years; when rival powers first arose, I was a commoner of Huai-you and raised an army to save the people.
translations.idiomatic: For eighteen years the heartland knew only turmoil. When the warlords first rose, I was a commoner of Huai-you and took up arms to deliver the people.

sentences.zh: 荷天之靈，授以文武諸臣，東渡江左，練兵養士，十有四年。

translations.literal: By Heaven's blessing I was given civil and military ministers; I crossed east to the lands south of the Yangzi, trained troops and nurtured scholars, for fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's favor gave me able ministers; I crossed the Yangzi to the southeast, drilled armies and gathered talent, for fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 西平漢王陳友諒，東縛吳王張士誠，南平閩、粵，戡定巴、蜀，北定幽、燕，奠安方夏，復我中國之舊疆。

translations.literal: In the west I pacified King Chen Youliang of Han; in the east I bound King Zhang Shicheng of Wu; in the south I pacified Min and Yue; in Ba and Shu I settled the realm; in the north I secured You and Yan; I settled the central lands and restored China's old frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: I crushed Chen Youliang in the west and Zhang Shicheng in the east, pacified Fujian and Guangdong in the south and Sichuan in the southwest, secured the north around Beijing, and restored the old borders of the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 朕為臣民推戴即皇帝位，定有天下之號曰大明，建元洪武，於今四年矣。

translations.literal: Urged on by officials and people I ascended the imperial throne, fixed the name of all-under-Heaven as Great Ming, and established the era Hongwu; it is now four years.
translations.idiomatic: At the urging of my subjects I took the throne, named the realm Great Ming, and proclaimed the Hongwu era—now in its fourth year.

sentences.zh: 凡四夷諸邦皆遣官告諭，惟爾拂菻隔越西海，未及報知。

translations.literal: All foreign states of the four directions have been notified by dispatched officials; only your Fulin, separated across the Western Sea, has not yet been informed.
translations.idiomatic: I have sent envoys to announce my accession to every foreign realm, but Fulin lies beyond the Western Sea and word has not yet reached you.

sentences.zh: 今遣爾國之民捏古倫齎詔往諭。

translations.literal: Now your countryman Niegu Lun is sent bearing the edict to instruct you.
translations.idiomatic: I now send your subject Niegu Lun back with this edict.

sentences.zh: 朕雖未及古先哲王，俾萬方懷德，然不可不使天下知朕平定四海之意，故茲詔告。」

translations.literal: Although I have not yet reached the ancient sage-kings in making the myriad regions cherish virtue, I must let all-under-Heaven know my intent to pacify the four seas; hence this edict."
translations.idiomatic: I am no sage-king of old who wins the world's hearts by virtue alone, yet I cannot let the world remain ignorant of my purpose in pacifying the realm—hence this proclamation."

sentences.zh: 已而覆命使臣普剌等齎敕書、彩幣招諭，其國乃遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Later, returning envoys including Pula carried imperial letters and colored silks to summon and instruct; the country then sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Niegu Lun returned, and later envoys led by Pula brought imperial letters and silks of invitation; Fulin then sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 後不復至。

translations.literal: Afterward they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: No further missions followed.

sentences.zh: 萬曆時，大西洋人至京師，言天主耶穌生於如德亞

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, a man of the Great Western Ocean reached the capital and said that the Lord of Heaven Jesus was born in Judea
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli era, a man from the Atlantic Ocean came to the capital and declared that Jesus, Lord of Heaven, was born in Judea

sentences.zh: 〈Judea，今巴勒斯坦地區中部的朱迪亞

translations.literal: 〈Judea, present-day Judea in the central Palestinian region
translations.idiomatic: 〈(Judea—the central hill country of present-day Palestine

translations.literal: (Judea)〉〉,
translations.idiomatic: Judea))〉,

sentences.zh: 即古大秦國也。

translations.literal: which is the ancient state of Da Qin.
translations.idiomatic: the old land known to China as Da Qin.

sentences.zh: 其國自開辟以來六千年，史書所載，世代相嬗，及萬事萬物原始，無不詳悉。

translations.literal: That country, since the opening of creation, has six thousand years; what the historical books record—the succession of ages and the origins of all things—is without exception detailed.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed their land had existed for six thousand years since creation, with histories recording every age and the origin of all things in exhaustive detail.

sentences.zh: 謂為天主肇生人類之邦，言頗誕謾不可信。

translations.literal: To call it the land where the Lord of Heaven first begat mankind—the words are rather wild and absurd and cannot be believed.
translations.idiomatic: Their claim that this was where God first created mankind struck the court as extravagant and incredible.

sentences.zh: 其物產、珍寶之盛，具見前史。

translations.literal: The abundance of its products and treasures is fully seen in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: The wealth of its products and treasures is already recorded in earlier dynastic histories.

sentences.zh: 意大里亞

translations.literal: Yidaliya
translations.idiomatic: Italia

sentences.zh: 意大里亞

translations.literal: Yidaliya
translations.idiomatic: Italia

sentences.zh: 〈即今義大利〉，

translations.literal: 〈namely present-day Italy〉,
translations.idiomatic: 〈present-day Italy〉,

sentences.zh: 居大西洋中，自古不通中國。

translations.literal: situated in the midst of the Great Western Ocean, from antiquity had no contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: lay in the Atlantic Ocean and had never had contact with China.

sentences.zh: 萬曆時，其國人利瑪竇至京師，為《萬國全圖》，言天下有五大洲。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, a man of that country, Matteo Ricci, reached the capital, compiled the Complete Map of Ten Thousand Countries, and said that under Heaven there are five great continents.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli era, Matteo Ricci of Italia came to the capital, drew the Complete Map of All Nations, and declared that the world comprised five great continents.

sentences.zh: 第一曰亞細亞洲，中凡百餘國，而中國居其一。

translations.literal: The first is called Asia; within it are more than a hundred states, and China occupies one.
translations.idiomatic: The first was Asia, containing more than a hundred realms of which China was one.

sentences.zh: 第二曰歐羅巴洲，中凡七十餘國，而意大里亞居其一。

translations.literal: The second is called Europe; within it are more than seventy states, and Italia occupies one.
translations.idiomatic: The second was Europe, with more than seventy realms including Italia.

sentences.zh: 第三曰利未亞洲，亦百餘國。

translations.literal: The third is called Libya; it too has more than a hundred states.
translations.idiomatic: The third was Libya—Africa—with more than a hundred realms as well.

sentences.zh: 第四曰亞墨利加洲，地更大，以境土相連，分為南北二洲。

translations.literal: The fourth is called America; the land is even larger, and because its territories connect, it is divided into northern and southern continents.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth was America, larger still, its connected landmass divided into North and South.

sentences.zh: 最後得墨瓦臘泥加洲為第五。

translations.literal: Last was obtained Magellanica as the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Magellanica, discovered last, formed the fifth.

sentences.zh: 而域中大地盡矣。

translations.literal: Thus the great lands within the realm were complete.
translations.idiomatic: In this way, they said, the earth was fully accounted for.

sentences.zh: 其說荒渺莫考，然其國人充斥中土，則其地固有之，不可誣也。

translations.literal: Their account is vast and remote and cannot be verified, yet since men of their country fill the Central Plain, that land must exist and cannot be denied.
translations.idiomatic: The account seemed fantastic and beyond proof, yet since their countrymen were already scattered across China, their homeland could hardly be dismissed as fiction.

sentences.zh: 大都歐羅巴諸國，悉奉天主耶穌教，而耶穌生於如德亞，其國在亞細亞洲之中，西行教於歐羅巴。

translations.literal: Most states of Europe all follow the Lord of Heaven Jesus teaching; Jesus was born in Judea, his country lies within Asia, and westward he taught in Europe.
translations.idiomatic: Most European states followed the teaching of Jesus, Lord of Heaven. Born in Judea in Asia, he carried his doctrine west into Europe.

sentences.zh: 其始生在漢哀帝元壽二年庚申，閱一千五百八十一年至萬曆九年，利瑪竇始泛海九萬里，抵廣州之香山澳，其教遂沾染中土。

translations.literal: He was first born in the gengshen year, the second year of Yuanshou of Han Emperor Ai; counting one thousand five hundred eighty-one years to the ninth year of Wanli, Matteo Ricci first crossed the sea ninety thousand li and reached Xiangshan Ao of Guangzhou, and the teaching then touched the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: They dated his birth to the second year of Yuanshou under Emperor Ai of Han (1 BCE). One thousand five hundred eighty-one years later, in Wanli 9 (1581), Ricci sailed ninety thousand li across the sea to Macao at Guangzhou, and the faith first took root in China.

sentences.zh: 至二十九年入京師，中官馬堂以其方物進獻，自稱大西洋人。

translations.literal: By the twenty-ninth year he entered the capital; the eunuch Ma Tang presented his local products as tribute, and he called himself a man of the Great Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 29 (1601) he reached Beijing; the eunuch Ma Tang presented his gifts to the throne, and Ricci styled himself a man of the Atlantic Ocean.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「《會典》止有西洋瑣裡國無大西洋，其真偽不可知。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "The Statutes only list the Western Ocean state of Choli and not the Great Western Ocean; whether this is genuine cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites reported: "The Statutes recognize Choli in the Western Ocean but not the Atlantic—his origin cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 又寄居二十年方行進貢，則與遠方慕義特來獻琛者不同。

translations.literal: Moreover, after dwelling as a resident for twenty years he then came to present tribute—this differs from distant realms that, admiring righteousness, come specially to offer gems.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he had lived here twenty years before offering tribute—hardly the same as envoys who voyage from afar out of admiration for our civilization.

sentences.zh: 且其所貢《天主》及《天主母圖》，既屬不經，而所攜又有神仙骨諸物。

translations.literal: Furthermore, what he presented—the Lord of Heaven and the Picture of the Lord of Heaven's Mother—are already unorthodox, and what he carried also included bones of immortals and other things.
translations.idiomatic: The images of the Lord of Heaven and his Mother that he presented were already heterodox, and he also carried saintly relics and the like.

sentences.zh: 夫既稱神仙，自能飛昇，安得有骨？

translations.literal: If they are called immortals, they can by themselves ascend in flight—how could there be bones?
translations.idiomatic: If these were truly immortals who ascended to heaven, how could their bones remain?

sentences.zh: 則唐韓愈所謂凶穢之餘，不宜入宮禁者也。

translations.literal: These are what Tang's Han Yu called the foul remnants of evil and ought not enter the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: They are precisely the "filthy remnants" Han Yu of Tang condemned—unfit for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 況此等方物，未經臣部譯驗，徑行進獻，則內臣混進之非，與臣等溺職之罪，俱有不容辭者。

translations.literal: Moreover, such local products, not having passed through this ministry's translation and inspection, were presented directly—then the inner officials' fault in mixing in presentation and this ministry's dereliction of duty both admit no excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, these objects reached the throne without our ministry's review or translation—the eunuchs' impropriety and our own negligence are alike indefensible.

sentences.zh: 及奉旨送部，乃不赴部審譯，而私寓僧舍，臣等不知其何意。

translations.literal: When ordered by imperial command to come to the ministry, he did not attend for examination and translation but lodged privately in a monk's quarters—we do not know his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to report to us, he refused examination and lodged instead at a monastery—we cannot fathom his purpose.

sentences.zh: 但諸番朝貢，例有回賜，其使臣必有宴賞，乞給賜冠帶還國，勿令潛居兩京，與中人交往，別生事端。」

translations.literal: Yet for all foreign tribute missions there are return gifts by precedent, and envoys must receive banquets and rewards; we beg that cap and belt be granted and he be sent home, and that he not be allowed to dwell secretly in the two capitals, associate with palace attendants, and give rise to other troubles."
translations.idiomatic: Foreign missions customarily receive return gifts and banquets; we ask that he be granted cap and belt and sent home, and not allowed to linger in the capitals consorting with eunuchs and stirring up trouble."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 八月又言：「臣等議令利瑪竇還國，候命五月，未賜綸音，毋怪乎遠人之郁病而思歸也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they again said: "We proposed sending Matteo Ricci home; he has awaited orders for five months without receiving an imperial decree—no wonder the distant man grows depressed and longs to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they wrote again: "We recommended sending Ricci home; he has waited five months without an answer—small wonder the foreigner grows ill with longing to return.

sentences.zh: 察其情詞懇切，真有不願尚方錫予，惟欲山棲野宿之意。

translations.literal: Observing his words, they are earnest; he truly seems unwilling to receive gifts from the imperial workshop and desires only to dwell in mountains and sleep in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: His pleas ring sincere: he wants no imperial bounty, only to live in mountain seclusion.

sentences.zh: 譬之禽鹿久羈，愈思長林豐草，人情固然。

translations.literal: It is like birds and deer long confined, ever longing for deep woods and lush grass—human feeling is naturally so.
translations.idiomatic: Like a deer long caged that yearns for open woods, his wish is only human nature.

sentences.zh: 乞速為頒賜，遣赴江西諸處，聽其深山邃谷，寄跡怡老。」

translations.literal: We beg that permission be quickly granted and he be sent to places in Jiangxi, allowing him in deep mountains and remote valleys to take lodging and live out his years in contentment."
translations.idiomatic: We beg a prompt decree sending him to Jiangxi, where he may retire to deep valleys and live out his days in peace."

sentences.zh: 亦不報。

translations.literal: Again no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Again there was no response.

sentences.zh: 已而帝嘉其遠來，假館授粲，給賜優厚。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor commended his coming from afar, lodged him and supplied grain, and granted generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor welcomed his long journey, lodged him at court, provisioned him generously, and favored him with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下重其人，咸與晉接。

translations.literal: From ministers and grandees downward all esteemed the man and all received and met with him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials high and low respected him and sought his company.

sentences.zh: 瑪竇安之，遂留居不去，以三十八年四月卒於京。

translations.literal: Ricci was content and therefore remained without leaving; in the fourth month of the thirty-eighth year he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ricci settled in and stayed; he died in Beijing in the fourth month of Wanli 38 (1610).

sentences.zh: 賜葬西郭外。

translations.literal: Burial was granted outside the western gate.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him burial outside the western gate.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月朔，日食。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, on the first day, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month that year, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 歷官推算多謬，朝議將修改。

translations.literal: The calendar officials' calculations were largely wrong, and court discussion turned to revision.
translations.idiomatic: The astronomical bureau's predictions had been widely wrong, and the court debated reforming the calendar.

sentences.zh: 明年，五官正周子愚言：「大西洋歸化人龐迪我、熊三拔等深明曆法。

translations.literal: The next year, Director of the Five Offices Zhou Ziyu said: "The naturalized men of the Great Western Ocean, Diego de Pantoja, Sabatino de Ursis, and others are deeply versed in calendrical methods.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Zhou Ziyu, Director of the Five Offices, reported: "Diego de Pantoja, Sabatino de Ursis, and other Atlantic converts are masters of calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 其所攜曆書，有中國載籍所未及者。

translations.literal: The calendrical books they carry contain matters not reached by China's recorded texts.
translations.idiomatic: Their astronomical texts contain methods not found in Chinese records.

sentences.zh: 當令譯上，以資採擇。」

translations.literal: They should be ordered translated and submitted for use in selection."
translations.idiomatic: They should be translated and submitted for the court's consideration."

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎翁正春等因請仿洪武初設回回曆科之例，令迪我等同測驗。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Weng Zhengchun and others therefore requested, following the early Hongwu precedent of establishing the Muslim calendrical school, that Pantoja and the others be ordered to conduct tests together.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Weng Zhengchun and others then asked that Pantoja and his colleagues be put to the test, as the Muslim calendrical bureau had been at the start of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 自瑪竇入中國後，其徒來益眾。

translations.literal: After Ricci entered China, his followers came in ever greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: After Ricci's arrival, his fellow missionaries came in growing numbers.

sentences.zh: 有王豐肅者，居南京，專以天主教惑眾，士大夫暨裡巷小民，間為所誘。

translations.literal: There was one Wang Fengsu, who dwelt in Nanjing and devoted himself to beguiling the masses with Catholic teaching; among gentry-officials and lane-and-alley common folk, some were led astray.
translations.idiomatic: One Wang Fengsu lived in Nanjing, preaching Catholicism and winning converts among scholars and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中徐如珂惡之。

translations.literal: Section Director of the Ministry of Rites Xu Ruke detested this.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ruke, a director in the Ministry of Rites, despised the movement.

sentences.zh: 其徒又自誇風土人物遠勝中華，如珂乃召兩人，授以筆札，令各書所記憶。

translations.literal: His followers also boasted that their land's customs and people far surpassed China; Ruke therefore summoned two men, gave them brush and paper, and ordered each to write what he remembered.
translations.idiomatic: When their disciples boasted that their homelands surpassed China in every way, Xu summoned two of them, gave them paper, and told each to write down what he recalled.

sentences.zh: 悉舛謬不相合，乃倡議驅斥。

translations.literal: All were erroneous and did not agree; he then initiated a proposal to drive them out.
translations.idiomatic: Their accounts contradicted each other entirely, and he began calling for their expulsion.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，與侍郎沈㴶、給事中晏文輝等合疏斥其邪說惑眾，且疑其為佛郎機假托，乞急行驅逐。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, together with Vice Minister Shen Jin, Supervising Secretary Yan Wenhui, and others, he jointly memorialized condemning their heterodox teachings for misleading the masses, and also suspecting them of being Portuguese impostors, begging that expulsion be carried out urgently.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 44 (1616), he joined Vice Minister Shen Jin, Supervising Secretary Yan Wenhui, and others in a memorial denouncing the sect's heresy and suspecting the missionaries of being Portuguese impostors, urging immediate expulsion.

sentences.zh: 禮科給事中余懋孳亦言：「自利瑪竇東來，而中國復有天主之教。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary of the Rites Section Yu Maozi also said: "Since Matteo Ricci came east, China again has the teaching of the Lord of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Maozi of the Rites Section also wrote: "Since Ricci came from the east, the Lord of Heaven's teaching has taken root in China.

sentences.zh: 乃留都王豐肅、陽瑪諾等，煽惑群眾不下萬人，朔望朝拜動以千計。

translations.literal: Yet in the southern capital Wang Fengsu, Yang Manuo, and others stir up the masses—no fewer than ten thousand; on new and full moons bowing in worship often reaches a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanjing, Wang Fengsu, Yang Manuo, and others have swayed more than ten thousand followers, with thousands gathering for worship at each new and full moon.

sentences.zh: 夫通番、左道並有禁。

translations.literal: Trade with foreigners and heterodox teachings are both prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Unauthorized foreign contact and heterodox teachings are both forbidden by law.

sentences.zh: 今公然夜聚曉散，一如白蓮、無為諸教。

translations.literal: Now they openly gather at night and disperse at dawn, just like the White Lotus, Wuwei, and other teachings.
translations.idiomatic: They now meet openly by night and disperse at dawn, in the manner of the White Lotus and Wuwei sects.

sentences.zh: 且往來壕鏡，與澳中諸番通謀，而所司不為遣斥，國家禁令安在？」

translations.literal: Moreover they travel to and from Haojing, conspiring with the various foreigners in Macao, yet the responsible offices do not drive them out—where is the state's prohibition?"
translations.idiomatic: They travel freely to Macao and consort with foreigners there, while the authorities do nothing—where, then, is the force of imperial law?"

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，至十二月令豐肅及迪我等俱遣赴廣東，聽還本國。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted their words; by the twelfth month he ordered Fengsu and Pantoja and the others all sent to Guangdong and allowed to return to their native countries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the memorial, and in the twelfth month ordered Fengsu, Pantoja, and the others sent to Guangdong and permitted to return home.

sentences.zh: 命下久之，遷延不行，所司亦不為督發。

translations.literal: Long after the order was issued, delay continued without execution, and the responsible offices also did not supervise departure.
translations.idiomatic: The order lingered unenforced for months, and the responsible offices never pressed for compliance.

sentences.zh: 四十六年四月，迪我等奏：「臣與先臣利瑪竇等十餘人，涉海九萬里，觀光上國，叨食大官十有七年。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the forty-sixth year, Pantoja and the others memorialized: "We, together with the late Matteo Ricci and more than ten others, crossed the sea ninety thousand li, came to observe the splendor of the upper country, and have presumptuously received great official provision for seventeen years.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Wanli 46 (1618), Pantoja and his colleagues petitioned: "We and the late Ricci—more than a dozen in all—crossed ninety thousand li of ocean to behold your civilization and have been fed at the state's table for seventeen years.

sentences.zh: 近南北參劾，議行屏斥。

translations.literal: Recently censors north and south have impeached them, and it was proposed to expel and exclude them.
translations.idiomatic: Recently censors from both capitals had impeached them and proposed their expulsion.

sentences.zh: 竊念臣等焚修學道，尊奉天主，豈有邪謀敢墮惡業。

translations.literal: We privately reflect that we burn incense and cultivate the Way, revering the Lord of Heaven—how could we harbor evil designs and dare fall into wicked karma?
translations.idiomatic: We who burn incense and study the Way, worshipping the Lord of Heaven, would never harbor evil designs or fall into wickedness.

sentences.zh: 惟聖明垂憐，候風便還國。

translations.literal: We only beg the sage brilliance to show pity and, when the wind is favorable, return to our country.
translations.idiomatic: We beg only for imperial mercy and a fair wind to carry us home.

sentences.zh: 若寄居海嶼，愈滋猜疑，乞並南都諸處陪臣，一體寬假。」

translations.literal: If we lodge on islands in the sea, suspicion will only increase; we beg that together with the attendant envoys in the southern capital and other places we may all receive uniform leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling on offshore isles would only breed suspicion; we ask that the attendant envoys in Nanjing and elsewhere receive the same clemency.

sentences.zh: 不報，乃怏怏而去。

translations.literal: No reply was given, and they departed in displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: They received no answer and left in displeasure.

sentences.zh: 豐肅尋變姓名，復入南京，行教如故，朝士莫能察也。

translations.literal: Fengsu soon changed his name and again entered Nanjing, practicing the teaching as before, and court gentlemen could not detect him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fengsu soon assumed another name, returned to Nanjing, and preached as before without detection by the court.

sentences.zh: 其國善制礮，視西洋更巨。

translations.literal: Their country is skilled at making cannon, larger than those of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: They excelled at casting cannon even larger than those of the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 既傳入內地，華人多效之，而不能用。

translations.literal: Once the method spread into the interior, many Chinese imitated it but could not make them work.
translations.idiomatic: Once the art reached the interior many Chinese copied it but could not make it effective.

sentences.zh: 天啟、崇禎間，東北用兵，數召澳中人入都，令將士學習，其人亦為盡力。

translations.literal: Between Tianqi and Chongzhen, when troops were used in the northeast, men from Macao were repeatedly summoned to the capital to teach the officers and soldiers, and those men also exerted themselves fully.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi and Chongzhen reigns, with war in the northeast, Macao gunners were repeatedly summoned to the capital to train the troops, and they gave their full effort.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，曆法益疏舛，禮部尚書徐光啟請令其徒羅雅谷、湯若望等，以其國新法相參較，開局纂修。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period the calendar method grew ever more loose and erroneous; Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi requested that his disciples Ruggieri, Schall, and others compare their country's new method and open a bureau to compile and revise.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen the calendar grew increasingly inaccurate; Xu Guangqi, Minister of Rites, asked Schall, Ruggieri, and others to compare their new methods and open a bureau to revise the calendar.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 久之書成，即以崇禎元年戊辰為歷元，名之曰《崇禎歷》。

translations.literal: After a long time the book was completed; the first year of Chongzhen, the wuchen year, was taken as the calendar origin, and it was named the Chongzhen Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished it took Chongzhen 1 (1628), year wuchen, as its epoch and was named the Chongzhen Calendar.

sentences.zh: 書雖未頒行，其法視《大統歷》為密，識者有取焉。

translations.literal: Although the book was not yet promulgated, its method was denser than the Great Unity Calendar, and the knowledgeable approved of it.
translations.idiomatic: Though never officially promulgated, its methods were finer than those of the Great Unity Calendar, and experts valued it.

sentences.zh: 其國人東來者，大都聰明特達之士，意專行教，不求祿利。

translations.literal: Those of their country who came east were mostly men of outstanding intelligence, intent solely on spreading the teaching and not seeking salary or profit.
translations.idiomatic: Those who came from the West were mostly brilliant men devoted to preaching, not seeking office or profit.

sentences.zh: 其所著書多華人所未道，故一時好異者咸尚之。

translations.literal: Their written works mostly treated what Chinese had not yet spoken of, so for a time all who delighted in the strange esteemed them.
translations.idiomatic: Their books treated matters Chinese scholars had not addressed, and for a time every lover of novelty admired them.

sentences.zh: 而士大夫如徐光啟、李之藻輩，首好其說，且為潤色其文詞，故其教驟興。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials such as Xu Guangqi and Li Zhizao were first to delight in their doctrine and even polished their literary phrasing, and therefore their teaching suddenly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials such as Xu Guangqi and Li Zhizao were the first to embrace their teaching and even polished their prose, so the faith spread swiftly.

sentences.zh: 時著聲中土者，更有龍華民、畢方濟、艾如略、鄧玉函諸人。

translations.literal: At the time others who made a name in China included Longobardo, Fabri, Aleni, and Terrenz.
translations.idiomatic: Others who won renown in China included Longobardo, Fabri, Aleni, and Terrenz.

sentences.zh: 華民、方濟、如略及熊三拔，皆意大里亞國人，玉函，熱而瑪尼國人，龐迪我，依西把尼亞國人，陽瑪諾，波而都瓦爾國人，皆歐羅巴洲之國也。

translations.literal: Longobardo, Fabri, Aleni, and Sabatino de Ursis were all men of Italy; Terrenz was a man of the German lands; Pantoja was a man of Spain; Yang Ma-no was a man of Portugal—all countries of Europe.
translations.idiomatic: Longobardo, Fabri, Aleni, and Sabatino de Ursis were Italians; Terrenz was German; Pantoja was Spanish; Yang Ma-no was Portuguese—all from Europe.

sentences.zh: 其所言風俗、物產多誇，且有《職方外紀》諸書在，不具述。

translations.literal: What they say of customs and products is often exaggerated, and since books such as the Record of Foreign Lands Beyond the Offices exist, they are not fully set forth here.
translations.idiomatic: Their accounts of customs and products are often exaggerated; works such as the Record of Foreign Lands Beyond the Offices already cover them, and they are not repeated here.
